papers.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Trajectory2Gym improves tool-use training by constructing interactions with compositional coverage and decision grounding rather than collecting successful trajectories.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. Even successful interactions may underrepresent multi-step dependencies or contain actions that are unjustified by the information visible to the agent at decision time. We identify two coupled requirements for effective trajectory supervision: compositional coverage, so that important observation-action dependencies are represented, and decision grounding, so that each supervised action is supported by the learner-visible interaction history. We introduce Trajectory2Gym, which constructs executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and derives supervision only from grounded decisions in their realized executions. Structural-support selection allocates the resulting experience, while parent-normalized supervised fine-tuning preserves the semantic interaction as the unit of training weight. This reframes trajectory generation as the deliberate construction of learnable interaction experience, rather than the collection of successful trajectories. Across five Qwen3 scales, Trajectory2Gym improves Tau1, Tau2, and BFCL at every tested scale, increasing the equal-weight three-benchmark mean by 16.9-29.8 percentage points. The gains are strongest in stateful and multi-turn interaction, where later decisions depend on earlier observations and feedback. Our results suggest that scaling tool-use agents depends not only on collecting more successful trajectories, but on constructing interactions whose dependencies are represented and whose decisions are learnable from the agent's visible history.

ru.title: Учим агентов не просто успешным траекториям, а обучаемому опыту взаимодействия
ru.desc: Статья представляет Trajectory2Gym, метод обучения LLM-агентов использованию инструментов (tool-use), который строит исполняемые взаимодействия вокруг недостаточно представленных композиционных структур, а не просто собирает успешные траектории. Ключевые принципы: компositional coverage, чтобы важные зависимости «наблюдение-действие» были отражены, и decision grounding, чтобы каждое действие опиралось на историю взаимодействия, видимую агенту. Супервизия (SFT с нормализацией по родительскому взаимодействию) извлекается только из обоснованных решений, а выбор структур выделяет ресурсы обучения. Эксперименты на моделях Qwen3 разных масштабов показывают рост качества на Tau1, Tau2 и BFCL примерно на 17–30 п.п., особенно в stateful и многошаговых сценариях.

en.title: Constructing Learnable Interactions for Better Tool-Use Training
en.desc: Trajectory2Gym enhances tool-use training by focusing on creating interactions that cover important observation-action relationships and ensuring decisions are based on visible information. Instead of relying solely on successful trajectories, it emphasizes the need for compositional coverage and decision grounding to improve learning. The method constructs executable interactions that highlight under-supported structures and derives supervision from grounded decisions during execution. This approach leads to significant performance improvements across various scales, particularly in scenarios where decisions depend on previous observations.

zh.title: 构建可学习的交互经验，超越成功轨迹的收集
zh.desc: Trajectory2Gym通过构建具有组合覆盖和决策基础的交互来改善工具使用训练，而不是仅仅收集成功的轨迹。成功的工具使用轨迹并不一定能提供有效的监督，因为它们可能无法充分代表多步骤的依赖关系。我们提出了两个有效轨迹监督的要求：组合覆盖和决策基础，以确保每个监督动作都有可见的交互历史支持。通过这种方法，Trajectory2Gym将轨迹生成重新定义为有意识地构建可学习的交互经验，而不是简单地收集成功的轨迹。

papers.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
papers.abstract: Abstract StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and hierarchical memory harness to enable proactive, intent-aware interaction with implicit and evolving user goals.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. However, prevailing methods largely rely on explicit requests while miss the implicit user intent (e.g., "where should I click next?" while a user navigate a website), meanwhile fail to update the state simultaneously as user requests might update continuously. These limitations make them less suited to intent-aware interaction in practical. To address these challenges, we introduce StreamVibe-Bench, a new benchmark serving as testbed for user intent interaction, with 4.1K evaluation samples and 85K training samples spanning explicit, implicit, and dynamic intents. Building on this benchmark, we develop StreamVibe-VL, a streaming proactive model that infers implicit user intents from continuous observations and dynamically tailors its interactions as these intents evolve. We further introduce StreamVibe-Harness, which maintains user intents as persistent states with a fleixble lifecycles via a hierarchical memory to track the latest user intent and environmental state. Our experiments reveal three key findings: (i) StreamVibe-VL preserves strong general video understanding while improving response timing and answer quality by 10.7% over other baselines; (ii) existing proactive models remain limited in understanding user intent and deciding when to respond, especially under implicit and dynamic intents; and (iii) StreamVibe-Harness further improves response consistency and adaptation over sustained interaction, resulting in a 12.3% gain in proactive interaction.

ru.title: Модель, которая угадывает, что вы хотите сделать дальше
ru.desc: Статья представляет StreamVibe — набор из бенчмарка StreamVibe-Bench, стриминговой vision-language модели StreamVibe-VL и системы StreamVibe-Harness. Бенчмарк содержит 4,1 тыс. примеров для оценки и 85 тыс. для обучения, охватывая явные, неявные и динамически меняющиеся намерения пользователя. Модель StreamVibe-VL выводит скрытые намерения из непрерывного видеопотока и адаптирует проактивные ответы по мере их эволюции, а Harness хранит намерения как персистентные состояния с помощью иерархической памяти. Эксперименты показывают прирост на 10,7% по точности и времени ответа и на 12,3% в проактивном взаимодействии, при сохранении сильного общего понимания видео.

en.title: Proactive Interaction through Implicit Intent Understanding
en.desc: StreamVibe presents a new benchmark and model for enhancing interaction between users and vision-language systems by focusing on implicit user intents. Traditional models often rely on explicit requests, which limits their ability to understand evolving user goals during interactions. StreamVibe-Bench provides a comprehensive dataset for evaluating these interactions, while StreamVibe-VL is designed to proactively infer user intents from ongoing observations. Additionally, StreamVibe-Harness utilizes a hierarchical memory system to maintain and adapt to user intents over time, leading to improved response quality and consistency in interactions.

zh.title: 主动感知用户意图的流式交互模型
zh.desc: StreamVibe提出了一种新的基准测试和流式视觉语言模型，旨在实现主动的、意图感知的用户交互。该模型能够从用户的持续观察中推断隐含意图，并根据这些意图的变化动态调整交互方式。通过引入层次记忆，StreamVibe-Harness能够持续跟踪用户意图和环境状态，从而提高响应的一致性和适应性。实验结果表明，StreamVibe在视频理解和响应质量上均优于现有模型，显著提升了主动交互的效果。

papers.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
papers.abstract: Abstract TraceTrial-Bench evaluates agent harness reliability across seven components using mechanism-oriented tasks, trajectory tracing, and failure attribution to compare harness designs and diagnose failures.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small LLM agents are increasingly used to solve real-world problems, and their effectiveness depends on both the underlying models and the harnesses that support their operation. However, most existing benchmarks focus on model capabilities and overall agent performance, with limited attention to the evaluation of agent harnesses. To address this gap, we introduce TraceTrial-Bench, which organizes harness reliability into seven components covering context, execution, governance, lifecycle, observability, tools, and verification. We construct 95 expert-level, mechanism-oriented tasks with executable or state-based ground truth to support semantically equivalent comparisons while preserving the native behavior of each harness. We design a Trajectory Tracing (TT) module to capture agent execution traces and introduce a two-layer evaluation framework that separately assesses agent performance and harness reliability. In addition, we design a Multi-source Evidence Acquisition (MEA) module to provide evidence from the agent context, harness, and execution environment for LLM-based evaluation, and develop a Failure Attribution (FA) module that uses explicit mechanism chains to support attribution at the run level. Across 4 harnesses, 9 models, and 95 tasks, our evaluation of 3,420 runs yields macro-averaged harness scores ranging from 59.8% to 72.0%, while 31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion. TraceTrial-Bench provides an auditable and reproducible foundation for comparing agent harnesses, diagnosing their failures, and studying how harness design interacts with model behavior.

ru.title: Успешный результат не всегда означает надёжного агента: оцениваем не только модель, но и её обвязку
ru.desc: Статья представляет TraceTrial-Bench — бенчмарк для оценки надёжности agent harness, то есть обвязки, которая поддерживает работу LLM-агентов, а не только самих моделей. Надёжность разбита на семь компонентов: контекст, выполнение, governance, жизненный цикл, observability, инструменты и верификация, а тестирование проводится на 95 экспертных задачах с исполняемой или state-based разметкой. Для анализа используются модуль Trajectory Tracing, двухуровневая оценка, модуль Multi-source Evidence Acquisition для LLM-as-a-judge и Failure Attribution на основе механистических цепочек. Эксперименты на 3 420 запусках показывают разброс оценок harness от 59.8% до 72.0%, а 31.1% успешных по задаче запусков всё же нарушают хотя бы один критерий надёжности.

en.title: Evaluating Agent Harness Reliability with TraceTrial-Bench
en.desc: TraceTrial-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to assess the reliability of agent harnesses used in machine learning tasks. It focuses on seven key components that influence harness performance, including context and execution. The framework includes a Trajectory Tracing module to track agent actions and a Multi-source Evidence Acquisition module to gather relevant data for evaluation. By analyzing 3,420 runs across various harnesses and models, TraceTrial-Bench provides insights into harness effectiveness and helps identify areas for improvement in agent design.

zh.title: 智能体支撑系统的可靠性评估工具
zh.desc: TraceTrial-Bench 是一个评估智能体支撑系统可靠性的工具，涵盖七个关键组件，包括上下文、执行、治理、生命周期、可观察性、工具和验证。该工具通过设计 95 个专家级的机制导向任务，支持对不同支撑系统的语义等效比较，同时保持各自的原生行为。我们还设计了轨迹追踪模块来捕捉智能体的执行轨迹，并引入了一个双层评估框架，分别评估智能体性能和支撑系统的可靠性。此外，TraceTrial-Bench 提供了可审计和可重复的基础，帮助比较智能体支撑系统、诊断其故障，并研究支撑系统设计如何与模型行为相互作用。

papers.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.abstract: Abstract DynaFlow enables adaptive multi-agent collaboration by letting a main agent synthesize executable workflows that coordinate sub-agents through structured execution and verification.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects. All sub-agents remain fixed, separating orchestration learning from executor capability improvement. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific question answering, and multi-hop retrieval, DynaFlow achieves 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.90 percentage points with the same Qwen3.5-27B backbone. Workflow analysis finds more explicit use, verification, and refinement of upstream outputs after training, highlighting cross-stage information flow as a key dimension of multi-agent orchestration.

ru.title: Агент сам строит план совместной работы и учится передавать информацию между шагами
ru.desc: В статье представлен DynaFlow — фреймворк, в котором основной агент (main agent) сам синтезирует исполняемые workflow-программы, координирующие подагентов последовательно или параллельно с проверкой результатов. Обучается только основной агент через supervised fine-tuning на дистиллированных траекториях с последующим дообучением на отфильтрованных примерах, тогда как подагенты остаются фиксированными. На шести бенчмарках (математические рассуждения, научный QA, multi-hop retrieval) DynaFlow достигает 88.08% точности в режиме Forced, превосходя лучший базовый метод на 10.90 п.п. на той же модели Qwen3.5-27B. Анализ показывает, что после обучения агент активнее использует, проверяет и уточняет выходы предыдущих этапов, что делает межэтапный информационный поток ключевым аспектом оркестрации multi-agent систем.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Adaptive Workflow Synthesis
en.desc: DynaFlow is a framework designed for adaptive collaboration among multiple agents by allowing a main agent to create executable workflows that manage sub-agents. This approach overcomes the limitations of fixed collaboration structures by enabling the main agent to generate task-specific programs that can execute tasks in sequence or parallel. The main agent learns through supervised fine-tuning, while the sub-agents remain unchanged, ensuring that the orchestration of tasks is distinct from the capabilities of the individual agents. DynaFlow demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy across various benchmarks, showcasing its effectiveness in enhancing multi-agent systems through better information flow and collaboration adaptation.

zh.title: DynaFlow：自适应多代理协作的新框架
zh.desc: DynaFlow 是一个框架，允许主要代理通过合成可执行的工作流来实现自适应的多代理协作。它使主要代理能够根据任务需求生成特定的程序，协调子代理的顺序或并行执行。通过监督微调主要代理，DynaFlow 在多个基准测试中表现出色，整体准确率达到 88.08%。该框架强调了信息流在多代理协调中的重要性，促进了上游输出的使用、验证和改进。

papers.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
papers.abstract: Abstract InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable simulation environment and benchmark to evaluate whether multimodal language models can reliably guide humans through physical tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. Powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs), egocentric AI assistants on wearable devices are bringing this dream within reach: they see what the user sees and give instructions for user's physical work when necessary. However, testing such assistance is challenging and usually requires real people. The expensive and rare real interaction data leaves a key question unanswered: Can today's MLLMs truly help people in physical world? To answer this question, we propose InteractiveWorld, the first verifiable environment for closed-loop interaction between human and AI assistant. Unlike existing robot-centric simulators, InteractiveWorld lets the assistant guide a human agent who observes the scene, understands instructions, and acts independently. It thus realistically simulates how AI assistant collaborates with human: the assistant instructs, the human acts, and the environment executes actions and updates what they see next. Building on it, we introduce InteractiveBench, the first dynamic benchmark for egocentric AI assistants, with 120 multi-turn tasks across six categories. In each task, the assistant guides the human in real time, and every instruction shapes the outcome, which is scored by verifiable, state-based rewards. Experiments with 12 frontier MLLMs show they are still far from reliable assistants. Even the strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, achieves at most 20% and 25% on long-horizon Guidance and Planning tasks, respectively. Overall, our work offers a verifiable platform and a rigorous evaluation set, laying a solid foundation for research on interactive MLLM assistants that truly help people in the physical world.

ru.title: Можно ли доверить MLLM роль живого проводника в реальном мире?
ru.desc: Авторы представляют InteractiveWorld — первую верифицируемую среду для замкнутого взаимодействия человека и AI-ассистента, где ассистент даёт инструкции, а человек действует в симулированном мире. На её основе создан InteractiveBench — динамический бенчмарк из 120 многошаговых задач в шести категориях, оценка которых проводится по проверяемым state-based наградам. Эксперименты с 12 передовыми мультимодальными LLM показали, что даже лучшая модель достигает лишь 20% и 25% на долгосрочных задачах Guidance и Planning. Работа задаёт прочную основу для исследований интерактивных MLLM-ассистентов, которые действительно помогают людям в физическом мире.

en.title: Evaluating AI Assistants in Real-World Tasks
en.desc: The paper introduces InteractiveWorld, a simulation environment designed to evaluate multimodal language models (MLLMs) in guiding humans through physical tasks. It addresses the challenge of testing AI assistants by allowing them to interact with human agents in a realistic setting, where the assistant provides instructions based on what the human sees. The study also presents InteractiveBench, a benchmark with 120 tasks that assess the performance of MLLMs in real-time guidance scenarios. Results indicate that current MLLMs, including the top-performing model, still struggle to reliably assist humans, highlighting the need for further research in this area.

zh.title: 构建可靠的AI助手，助力人类物理任务
zh.desc: InteractiveWorld是一个可验证的模拟环境，用于评估多模态语言模型（MLLMs）在指导人类完成物理任务方面的可靠性。该环境允许AI助手与人类代理进行闭环互动，模拟真实的协作过程。通过引入InteractiveBench，我们提供了一个动态基准，包含120个多轮任务，评估AI助手在实时指导中的表现。实验结果表明，目前的MLLMs仍然远未成为可靠的助手，尤其在长时间的指导和规划任务中表现不佳。

papers.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract The paper proposes a unified framework for work agents that integrates foundation models with runtime harnesses to execute complex digital tasks reliably, introducing dimensions of persistence and openness alongside capability families and evaluation metrics.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

ru.title: Надежные AI-агенты: от генерации информации к выполнению работы
ru.desc: Статья предлагает единую系统-level рамку для work agents, которые объединяют foundation models и runtime harnesses для надежного выполнения сложных цифровых задач. Авторы вводят два измерения, work persistence и work openness, а также классифицируют цифровую работу на пять форм по масштабу и организации задач. Выделены пять ключевых capability families и рассмотрены подходы к model optimization, harness optimization и их совместной оптимизации. Наконец, анализируются существующие метрики оценки по результатам работы и обсуждаются направления будущих исследований, включая длительное делегирование работы и адаптацию к открытым средам.

en.title: Empowering Work Agents for Reliable Digital Task Execution
en.desc: This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for work agents that combines foundation models with runtime harnesses to perform complex digital tasks effectively. It emphasizes the importance of two new dimensions: work persistence and work openness, which help define the conditions under which agents operate. The authors categorize digital work into five types based on task scope and organization, and identify five essential capability families necessary for reliable task execution. Additionally, the paper critiques existing evaluation methods and suggests future research directions to enhance the adaptability and effectiveness of work agents in dynamic environments.

zh.title: 统一框架：提升工作代理的可靠性与效率
zh.desc: 本文提出了一个统一的框架，用于工作代理，结合基础模型和运行时工具，以可靠地执行复杂的数字任务。随着基础模型从信息生成演变为数字工作执行，代理能够跨工具、应用和工作流程完成复杂任务。我们引入了工作持久性和工作开放性两个维度，来描述工作条件，并根据任务范围和组织将数字工作分类为五种形式。最后，本文还探讨了未来的研究方向，包括持续的工作委派、适应开放环境以及工作执行与能力提升之间的互动。

papers.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract A new benchmark evaluates whether LLM agents improve through repeated professional tasks with feedback, revealing limited sustained learning in current frontier models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.

ru.title: Современные LLM-агенты пока плохо учатся на собственном опыте
ru.desc: Авторы представляют бенчмарк Continual Learning Exam (CLE) для оценки непрерывного обучения LLM-агентов на основе накопленного опыта в реальных профессиональных задачах. Набор содержит 120 задач, каждая из которых разбита на пять уровней, которые открываются последовательно, а поздние уровни опираются на опыт предыдущих. Оценку выполняет отдельный LLM-агент по рубрикам, написанным экспертами, и сравниваются режимы без обратной связи и с диагностикой и одной ревизией. Результаты показывают, что обратная связь даёт небольшой прирост, но лучшая система проходит лишь 47,7% уровней, что указывает на слабую способность современных frontier-моделей к устойчивому обучению на опыте.

en.title: Unlocking Learning Potential in LLMs with Continual Learning Exam
en.desc: This paper introduces the Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a benchmark designed to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) can learn from experience over time. It consists of 120 tasks organized into a five-level ladder, covering various professional roles and requiring agents to build on their previous knowledge to progress. The study finds that while providing feedback and allowing revisions can improve performance, current LLMs struggle with sustained learning, achieving only moderate success in completing tasks. The CLE serves as a tool not only for assessment but also for enhancing the continual learning abilities of LLMs through post-training.

zh.title: 持续学习的挑战与机遇
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种新的基准测试，旨在评估大型语言模型（LLM）在重复专业任务中通过反馈是否能够持续学习。持续学习是指LLM代理能够通过经验获取、精炼和应用知识，同时保留有用的先前知识。研究表明，当前的前沿模型在持续学习方面表现有限，尽管提供了反馈和修订的机会，但最佳系统仅能完成47.7%的任务级别。该基准测试由50多位领域专家开发，包含120个任务，旨在测量基于经验的改进，强调了现有LLM在经验学习中的挑战。

papers.title: WorldCast: World-Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Control
papers.abstract: Abstract CLACT and WorldCast enable consistent character video generation under large-angle camera motions by combining 3D point-cloud guidance with geometry-aligned memory attention.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Precise camera control is essential for cinematic character video generation, yet existing methods struggle to follow large-angle trajectories with combined rotation, translation, and radius variation from arbitrary initial azimuths. Such viewpoint changes also reveal character regions unseen in the initial frame, causing geometric distortions, appearance degradation, and identity drift. To systematically study these coupled challenges, we introduce CLACT, a large-scale Character-centric dataset and benchmark covering diverse Large-Angle Camera Trajectories, with accurate camera geometry and multi-view character observations for training and evaluation. We further propose WorldCast, a framework for world-consistent character video generation under diverse large-angle camera motions. Specifically, we back-project the initial frame into a 3D point cloud using estimated depth, align the point-cloud scale with the target camera trajectory, and render it along the trajectory to obtain explicit geometric guidance and coverage masks. To complement the incomplete character information, we introduce Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention (GAMA). Using relative camera poses estimated jointly from the initial frame and multi-view character anchors, we express anchor and target-view geometry in a common coordinate frame. GAMA uses this geometric alignment to guide the retrieval and injection of view-relevant character features during generation. Evaluations across diverse large-angle camera trajectories demonstrate accurate trajectory following while preserving character geometry, appearance, and identity.

ru.title: Персонаж остаётся собой при любом ракурсе камеры
ru.desc: Статья представляет CLACT — крупный датасет и бенчмарк для генерации видео с персонажами при больших углах поворота камеры. Метод WorldCast строит 3D point cloud из первого кадра по оценке глубины, масштабирует его под целевую траекторию камеры и рендерит для получения геометрических подсказок и масок покрытия. Для восполнения невидимых в первом кадре областей персонажа используется механизм GAMA (Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention), который через относительные позы камеры выравнивает геометрию и извлекает релевантные признаки. Результаты показывают точное следование траектории камеры при сохранении геометрии, внешнего вида и идентичности персонажа.

en.title: Consistent Character Video Generation with Large-Angle Camera Motion
en.desc: This paper presents CLACT and WorldCast, two innovations aimed at improving character video generation when the camera moves at large angles. The methods address challenges like geometric distortions and identity drift that occur when the camera changes position significantly. CLACT is a dataset that helps train models by providing diverse camera trajectories and accurate character observations. WorldCast uses 3D point-cloud guidance and Geometry-Aligned Memory Attention to ensure that characters maintain their appearance and identity throughout the video, even with complex camera movements.

zh.title: 大角度摄像机运动下的一致角色视频生成
zh.desc: 本文介绍了CLACT和WorldCast，这两个方法可以在大角度摄像机运动下生成一致的角色视频。通过结合3D点云引导和几何对齐记忆注意力，解决了现有方法在复杂运动下的挑战。CLACT是一个大型角色中心数据集，涵盖多样的大角度摄像机轨迹，用于训练和评估。WorldCast框架则通过3D点云和几何对齐技术，确保在不同视角下生成的角色视频保持几何形状、外观和身份的一致性。

papers.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
papers.abstract: Abstract AMBIT is a unified framework that generates and edits first-order ambisonics audio by coupling autoregressive scene planning with rectified-flow rendering, using a specialized continuous VAE and on-policy self-distillation to preserve spatial structure and acoustic fidelity.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. For editing, plans specify what to change and retain, while reference audio supplies further acoustic detail. We present AMBIT, a unified framework for native First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) generation and editing with three connected contributions. First, a shared Transfusion backbone couples autoregressive planning with rectified-flow rendering through executable ScenePlans that specify source content, activity, and 3D trajectories. For editing, the plan describes the full target scene, including retained sources; contrastive features ground the requested change, while full reference latents supply residual acoustic detail for preservation. Second, an FOA-aware continuous VAE combines shared-decoder omnidirectional recovery, asymmetric grouped KL, and spatial covariance matching to preserve content and inter-channel structure. Third, joint Transfusion on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) refines planning on student-generated prefixes and rendering at sampling states reached under student plans, with target-conditioned teachers supervising both modes of the shared student. Evaluations across speech, music, and sound show improved generation content and spatial quality, acoustic fidelity during instruction-guided editing, and unedited-source preservation over the compared baselines. Project page: https://wjm-george.github.io/AMBIT/

ru.title: Объёмный звук по инструкции: планируй сцену и рендерь её целиком
ru.desc: Статья представляет AMBIT — единую модель для генерации и редактирования пространственного аудио в формате First-Order Ambisonics (FOA). Авторское решение объединяет авторегрессионное планирование сцены (ScenePlan с источниками, активностью и 3D-траекториями) и рендеринг через rectified flow на общем бэкбоне Transfusion. Для точного сохранения пространственной структуры используется специализированный непрерывный VAE с асимметричным grouped KL и согласованием пространственной ковариации. Обучение дополнительно усиливается joint on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), где целевые учителя направляют student-модель на собственных траекториях, и модель показывает улучшение качества на речи, музыке и звуках.

en.title: AMBIT: Revolutionizing Spatial Audio Generation and Editing
en.desc: AMBIT is a framework designed for generating and editing first-order ambisonics audio, which is a type of spatial audio. It combines autoregressive scene planning with rectified-flow rendering to maintain the spatial structure and sound quality. The framework uses a continuous Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to ensure that the audio content remains coherent and retains its acoustic fidelity during editing. Evaluations show that AMBIT outperforms existing methods in generating high-quality audio and preserving the original sound sources.

zh.title: AMBIT：统一的第一阶环绕声生成与编辑框架
zh.desc: AMBIT是一个统一的框架，用于生成和编辑第一阶环绕声（FOA）音频。它通过自回归场景规划与修正流渲染相结合，使用专门的连续变分自编码器（VAE）和在线自蒸馏技术，保持空间结构和声学保真度。该框架包括三个主要贡献：共享的Transfusion骨干网络、FOA感知的连续VAE，以及联合的在线自蒸馏。通过这些技术，AMBIT在语音、音乐和声音生成方面展示了更好的内容生成和空间质量。

papers.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
papers.abstract: Abstract AV-FABLE introduces a long-form audio-visual benchmark for sparse manipulations, showing that frozen perception features of audio-visual large language models contain forensic evidence best recovered via separate temporal decoders rather than language outputs.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Localized AI manipulations in long-form videos often affect brief events within otherwise authentic content, making video-level classification insufficient for forensic analysis. Existing audio-visual deepfake benchmarks largely focus on short talking-head clips, while long-form temporal forensics remains predominantly visual. We introduce AV-FABLE, a dual-timeline benchmark for sparse manipulations in open-scene long-form audio-visual videos. AV-FABLE contains 16,650 pristine--manipulated twin pairs (998 hours) created with 27 editing configurations, with separate audio and visual timelines that enable modality-specific temporal localization and expose errors hidden by joint-timeline evaluation. On AV-FABLE, zero-shot prompting of audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) yields near-chance detection and poor temporal localization. In contrast, supervised readouts of their frozen perception features recover strong forensic signals, suggesting manipulation evidence is encoded in these representations but not effectively exposed through language outputs. Motivated by this observation, we propose NFSR(Native Forensics via Separated Readouts), which reads frozen AV-LLM features with separate audio and visual temporal decoders. NFSR achieves the best audio-visual localization performance in-domain and across all three out-of-distribution settings, including transfer to held-out videos from an external long-video forensic benchmark. AV-FABLE, code, and model weights will be publicly released.

ru.title: Улики манипуляций скрыты в признаках AV-LLM, а не в их ответах
ru.desc: В статье представлен AV-FABLE — новый бенчмарк для длинных аудиовизуальных видео с локальными (sparse) манипуляциями, где аудио и видео имеют отдельные временные шкалы. Показано, что zero-shot промптинг AV-LLM дает почти случайное качество детекции, однако supervised-классификаторы поверх замороженных признаков (frozen features) извлекают сильные forensic-сигналы. На основе этого предложен метод NFSR, который использует раздельные временные декодеры для аудио и визуальной части и достигает лучшей точности локализации как in-domain, так и на out-of-distribution данных. Код, модели и датасет планируется опубликовать.

en.title: Unlocking Forensic Insights in Long-Form Audio-Visual Content
en.desc: The paper introduces AV-FABLE, a new benchmark designed for analyzing sparse manipulations in long-form audio-visual content. It highlights that traditional methods using audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) struggle with detecting manipulations effectively, especially when relying on language outputs. Instead, the authors propose using separate temporal decoders to analyze frozen perception features, which can better reveal forensic evidence of manipulations. The proposed method, Native Forensics via Separated Readouts (NFSR), demonstrates superior performance in localizing audio-visual manipulations compared to existing techniques.

zh.title: AV-FABLE：长格式音视频的稀疏操作基准
zh.desc: AV-FABLE是一个用于稀疏操作的长格式音视频基准，展示了音视频大型语言模型的冻结感知特征包含最佳的取证证据。这些证据通过独立的时间解码器而非语言输出得到更好的恢复。现有的音视频深伪基准主要集中在短视频片段，而长格式的时间取证仍然主要依赖视觉信息。我们提出的NFSR方法通过分离的音频和视觉时间解码器读取冻结的AV-LLM特征，显著提高了音视频定位性能。

papers.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
papers.abstract: Abstract FORK jointly optimizes recall and precision via rubric-driven necessity credits and factual grading to improve response quality and reduce verbosity in reinforcement learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. As a result, RL-trained models produce responses that are more complete but also more verbose and contain more unnecessary or factually incorrect content, leading them to be less preferred than responses from the base model. To address this issue, we present the FORK reward, which jointly optimizes recall and a novel precision objective, which requires each unit of a model response to be both necessary and factually correct, as measured by rubric-driven necessity credits and a factual-correctness grader, respectively. Our experimental results show that FORK outperforms existing rubric-based RL methods and achieves Pareto-optimal performance that balances rubric coverage and overall response quality. Compared to the original recall-based reward, FORK substantially improves precision and reduces response length while achieving similar rubric coverage, which leads to significantly higher win rate compared to the base policy (e.g., from 10.6% to 68.0% on RubricHub-Medical and from 22.1% to 74.1% on HealthBench).

ru.title: Полнота без воды: точность и полнота вместе в обучении LLM
ru.desc: В статье предлагается новая функция вознаграждения FORK для обучения с подкреплением (reinforcement learning) на задачах без верифицируемых ответов, где награда основана на rubric-based оценке. Классические rubric-based награды поощряют только полноту (recall), из-за чего LLM становятся многословными и допускают больше лишних и фактических ошибок. FORK совместно оптимизирует recall и новую метрику precision, которая требует, чтобы каждая единица ответа была необходимой (по rubric-driven necessity credits) и фактически корректной (по factual-correctness grader). Эксперименты показывают, что FORK достигает Парето-оптимального баланса между покрытием rubric и общим качеством, заметно улучшая precision, сокращая длину ответов и повышая win rate по сравнению с базовой моделью на RubricHub-Medical и HealthBench.

en.title: FORK: Balancing Recall and Precision for Better Responses
en.desc: The FORK method enhances response quality in reinforcement learning by optimizing both recall and precision through a new reward system. It uses rubric-driven necessity credits to ensure that each part of a response is essential and factually accurate. Traditional models often focus too much on recall, resulting in verbose and less accurate outputs. By balancing recall with a precision objective, FORK achieves better overall performance, leading to shorter, more accurate responses that are preferred over those generated by previous models.

zh.title: 优化召回与精确，提升响应质量
zh.desc: FORK是一种新型的奖励机制，旨在通过优化召回率和精确度来提高强化学习中的响应质量。它使用基于评分标准的必要性信用和事实评分来减少冗长的内容。传统的奖励机制往往只关注召回率，导致生成的响应虽然完整，但往往冗长且包含不必要或不准确的信息。FORK通过同时优化召回率和精确度，显著提高了响应的质量和简洁性，实验结果表明其性能优于现有的方法。

papers.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
papers.abstract: Abstract Δτ-Bench evaluates agent adaptability to evolving tool ecosystems, and Steward improves sustained success through incremental skill maintenance and dynamic provisioning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small In this paper, we introduce Δτ-Bench, an executable agent benchmark that models the structural evolution of large tool ecosystems. In Δτ-Bench, independently evolving services continually reshape how tasks can be accomplished: familiar tools may disappear or be replaced, while more efficient alternatives emerge amid overlapping functionality and noisy documentation. Against this moving capability frontier, we evaluate whether agents can proactively discover efficient tool-use paths and promptly revise their accumulated procedural knowledge, bringing together demands that existing benchmarks fail to examine. Δτ-Bench comprises 1,588 validated multi-turn tasks across 42 domains and six successive ecosystem states generated through capability-preserving transformations. Our evaluation shows that even the strongest evaluated model or harness achieves only 42.3% task success, while initial gains from existing skill-learning methods can not consistently translate into better adaptation as the ecosystem evolves. These findings motivate Steward, an ecosystem manager that jointly manages tools and procedural knowledge through incremental skill maintenance and dynamic provisioning during task execution. Experiments show that Steward sustains higher task success across ecosystem changes with lower skill-maintenance overhead, while improving both recovery from disrupted workflows and adoption of more efficient alternatives.

ru.title: Агент, который не теряется, когда меняется мир инструментов
ru.desc: В статье представлен Δτ-Bench — бенчмарк для LLM-агентов, который моделирует эволюцию больших экосистем инструментов, где сервисы меняются, исчезают или заменяются более эффективными аналогами. Оценка показала, что даже лучшие модели решают лишь 42,3% задач, а существующие методы skill learning плохо адаптируются к изменениям среды. Авторы предлагают Steward — менеджер экосистемы, который совместно управляет инструментами и процедурными знаниями агента через инкрементальное обновление навыков и динамическое предоставление инструментов во время выполнения задачи. Эксперименты показывают, что Steward поддерживает высокую успешность задач при изменениях экосистемы, снижает затраты на обслуживание навыков и лучше восстанавливается после сбоев и переходит на более эффективные инструменты.

en.title: Adapting Agents to Evolving Tool Ecosystems
en.desc: This paper presents Δτ-Bench, a benchmark designed to assess how well agents adapt to changing tool ecosystems. It highlights the challenges agents face as tools evolve, including the disappearance of familiar tools and the emergence of new, more efficient ones. The study reveals that even advanced models struggle to achieve high task success rates in this dynamic environment. To address these challenges, the paper introduces Steward, a system that enhances agents' adaptability by managing tools and procedural knowledge effectively during task execution.

zh.title: 提升代理适应性的工具生态系统评估
zh.desc: 本文介绍了Δτ-Bench，这是一个可执行的代理基准，旨在评估代理在不断变化的工具生态系统中的适应能力。该基准模拟了大型工具生态系统的结构演变，评估代理是否能够主动发现高效的工具使用路径，并及时修订其程序知识。研究表明，即使是最强的模型在任务成功率上也仅达到42.3%，而现有的技能学习方法在生态系统演变中并不能持续带来更好的适应性。为此，提出了Steward，一个生态系统管理器，通过增量技能维护和动态资源配置来提高任务执行的成功率。

papers.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: Abstract Principia is an LLM-based framework that builds and iteratively refines scientific principles during inference to accelerate discovery across molecular and biological tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Scientific discovery requires identifying the scientific principles underlying observed phenomena to guide further investigation. As these empirical principles are often unknown in complex discovery processes, they are constructed via a hypotheses-to-principle pipeline to obtain recurring causalities from progressively accumulated observations during test-time discovery. However, constructing this knowledge requires substantial domain expertise, time, and effort, making this translation stage a bottleneck for scientific discovery. To address this limitation, we propose Principia, an LLM-based framework that constructs and continually refines scientific principles at test time. Drawing on how human researchers develop principles, Principia forms comparative causal hypotheses from related inputs and their observed outcomes, then synthesizes recurring relationships across these hypotheses into inductive principles. By applying the constructed hypotheses and inductive principles to the task, it obtains new observations, revises the hypotheses used based on these new observations, and reconstructs principles from the updated hypotheses, allowing scientific knowledge to continuously evolve throughout test-time discovery. Across benchmarks spanning molecular optimization, protein engineering, gene perturbation, and molecular property prediction, Principia outperforms baselines relying on internal knowledge, external sources, or experience summaries, while generating principles that are plausible and consistent with the scientific literature, demonstrating its effectiveness in constructing and refining task-specific hypotheses and principles at test time for scientific discovery. Our code is available at https://github.com/DongkiKim95/Principia.

ru.title: Научные принципы, которые учатся прямо во время открытия
ru.desc: Статья представляет Principia — фреймворк на базе LLM, который строит и постепенно уточняет научные принципы прямо во время инференса. Система формулирует сравнительные причинно-следственные гипотезы по связанным входам и их результатам, а затем обобщает повторяющиеся зависимости в индуктивные принципы. Эти принципы применяются к задаче, новые наблюдения используются для пересмотра гипотез и восстановления принципов, что позволяет знаниям непрерывно эволюционировать. На задачах молекулярной оптимизации, инженерии белков, генетических возмущений и предсказания свойств молекул Principia превосходит базовые подходы и даёт правдоподобные принципы, согласованные с научной литературой.

en.title: Accelerating Scientific Discovery with LLMs: The Principia Framework
en.desc: Principia is a framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to create and improve scientific principles during the process of discovery in molecular and biological tasks. It addresses the challenge of identifying underlying scientific principles by employing a hypotheses-to-principle pipeline that extracts causal relationships from observations made during experiments. This iterative process allows Principia to refine its understanding of scientific principles as new data is gathered, mimicking how human researchers develop knowledge. The framework has shown superior performance in various scientific benchmarks, demonstrating its ability to generate plausible and consistent principles that enhance scientific discovery.

zh.title: 基于LLM的科学原理构建与优化
zh.desc: Principia是一个基于大型语言模型（LLM）的框架，旨在通过推理过程构建和不断完善科学原理，从而加速分子和生物任务的发现。该框架通过假设到原理的管道，利用逐步积累的观察结果提取因果关系，解决科学发现过程中常见的知识构建瓶颈。Principia模拟人类研究者的思维方式，形成比较因果假设，并将这些假设中的重复关系综合为归纳原理。通过在测试过程中应用这些构建的假设和原理，Principia能够不断修正和重建科学知识，推动科学发现的进程。

papers.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
papers.abstract: Abstract Qwen-Image-PE improves text-to-image prompts via two-stage training with caption-based reverse distillation and groupwise design rewards, scaling across data, model size, and information density.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Learning visual design is essential for prompt enhancement (PE) to turn underspecified user requests into coherent visual specifications for text-to-image (T2I) generation. Existing methods preserve user intent and improve overall visual appeal, with less explicit emphasis on fine-grained design dimensions. To address this gap, we introduce Qwen-Image-PE, which learns visual design through two-stage training. Supervised fine-tuning with Caption-Based Reverse Distillation (CRD) uses dense captions of well-designed images as design supervision. Reinforcement learning with Groupwise Design Reward (GDR) jointly compares all candidate images for the same request to refine lighting, composition, layout, and detail. On Qwen-Image-Bench with Qwen-Image-2.1, Qwen-Image-PE-397B improves over original requests by 7.81 points, while Qwen-Image-PE-9B outperforms all evaluated PE baselines. Further evaluations show gains in visual design, aesthetics, image quality, and human preference. We find that PE scales along three axes: training data, model size, and information density, with sufficient information density as a prerequisite for effective enhancement. Moreover, we demonstrate that Qwen-Image-PE generalizes to four additional T2I backbones, even surpassing native prompt enhancers on HunyuanImage-2.1 and FLUX 3 Image Klein. We release Qwen-Image-PE-9B at https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-PE-T2I.

ru.title: Обучаем промпты думать как дизайнер
ru.desc: Статья представляет Qwen-Image-PE, модель для улучшения промптов (prompt enhancement) для генерации изображений по тексту, которая учится визуальному дизайну в два этапа. На первом этапе используется supervised fine-tuning с Caption-Based Reverse Distillation, где в качестве супервизии выступают плотные описания хорошо оформленных изображений. На втором этапе применяется reinforcement learning с Groupwise Design Reward, который сравнивает все кандидаты для одного запроса и улучшает освещение, композицию, верстку и детали. Авторы показывают, что качество растет с увеличением объема данных, размера модели и плотности информации, а метод хорошо переносится на другие T2I-модели.

en.title: Enhancing Visual Design in Text-to-Image Generation
en.desc: Qwen-Image-PE is a novel approach to enhance text-to-image (T2I) generation by employing a two-stage training process that includes Caption-Based Reverse Distillation (CRD) and Groupwise Design Reward (GDR). This method focuses on improving visual design by using detailed captions from well-designed images as guidance during training. By comparing multiple candidate images for the same prompt, GDR helps refine aspects like lighting and composition, leading to better overall image quality. The results show significant improvements in visual appeal and user satisfaction, demonstrating that effective prompt enhancement can scale with data, model size, and information density.

zh.title: 提升文本到图像生成的视觉设计
zh.desc: Qwen-Image-PE是一种改进文本到图像生成的技术，通过两阶段训练来增强提示。它使用基于标题的反向蒸馏和组设计奖励来优化视觉设计，使用户的模糊请求转化为清晰的视觉规范。该方法通过监督微调和强化学习来提升图像的光照、构图、布局和细节。实验结果表明，Qwen-Image-PE在视觉设计、美学和图像质量方面均有显著提升，且能够在多个文本到图像模型上有效推广。

papers.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Abstract HiP3R uses a hierarchical pose graph to merge local video reconstructions into globally consistent camera trajectories and 3D geometry without retraining.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks. This division produces independent local reconstructions with inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate estimates of shared cameras. Achieving global consistency requires propagating constraints from adjacent overlaps and distant revisits across the sequence. This requirement naturally motivates pose graph optimization. However, the choice of graph level creates a trade-off. Chunk-level graphs efficiently resolve scale drift and close large loops. Yet, their rigid transformations cannot correct internal errors or conflicting frame predictions. Conversely, frame-level optimization offers local flexibility, but scaling it globally is computationally expensive and can break metric scale. HiP3R resolves this trade-off using a hierarchical pose graph. HiP3R first optimizes a robust chunk-level Sim(3) graph to establish the global layout and scale. It then holds this layout fixed and estimates one shared SE(3) camera per frame, turning overlapping window predictions into a single trajectory. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of HiP3R in improving camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction. Our method applies to both chunk-based and streaming backends without additional training or fine-tuning. The codes are available at https://kkakkkka.github.io/HiP3R.

ru.title: Единая траектория камеры из разрозненных кусочков видео
ru.desc: Статья представляет HiP3R — метод, который объединяет локальные 3D-реконструкции коротких видеоотрезков в глобально согласованные траектории камеры и геометрию сцены без дополнительного обучения. Длинные видео разбиваются на перекрывающиеся чанки, что даёт несогласованные системы координат и дублирующиеся оценки камер, а глобальную согласованность обеспечивает pose graph optimization. HiP3R использует иерархический граф: сначала оптимизируется chunk-level граф Sim(3) для масштаба и общей раскладки, затем фиксируется эта раскладка и оценивается единая SE(3)-камера для каждого кадра. Метод работает как с chunk-based, так и со streaming-моделями и показывает улучшения на нескольких бенчмарках.

en.title: Hierarchical Pose Graph for Consistent 3D Reconstruction
en.desc: HiP3R is a method that improves the consistency of camera trajectories and 3D geometry in video reconstructions by using a hierarchical pose graph. It combines local reconstructions from overlapping video chunks into a global framework without needing to retrain the models. The approach balances the efficiency of chunk-level optimization with the flexibility of frame-level adjustments, allowing for accurate camera motion estimation. Experiments show that HiP3R effectively enhances the quality of 3D reconstructions across various benchmarks.

zh.title: HiP3R：优化视频重建的层次化姿态图
zh.desc: HiP3R是一种使用层次化姿态图的方法，可以将局部视频重建合并为全局一致的相机轨迹和三维几何形状，而无需重新训练。该方法通过前馈模型准确估计相机运动和三维几何，但由于计算和内存成本，无法直接对包含成千上万帧的序列进行推断。为了实现全局一致性，HiP3R通过相邻重叠和远程重访之间传播约束来解决局部重建的不一致性。最终，HiP3R通过优化层次化姿态图，成功平衡了局部灵活性和全局一致性之间的权衡。

papers.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
papers.abstract: Abstract This survey defines recursive self-improvement and organizes trustworthy advancement requirements into improvement validity, constraint preservation, and oversight across recursive update stages.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) extends this process to inductive biases and to the mechanisms that govern future updates, which can themselves be revised and reused across improvement cycles. Yet self-modification alone does not guarantee trustworthy improvement. Reported gains may reflect flawed evaluations, previously acquired capabilities may deteriorate, and compliance with behavioral constraints may weaken. Compromised artifacts or sensitive information may also persist in successor systems. Changes to improvement mechanisms may invalidate earlier verification results and make human oversight less effective. This survey presents an operational definition and process framework for RSI and organizes the requirements for trustworthy RSI into four interconnected themes: genuine and sustained improvement; behavioral constraints, alignment, and fairness; system security and privacy; and transparency and controllability. We examine these themes from three perspectives: Improvement Validity, Constraint Preservation, and Effective Oversight. This analysis covers improvement diagnosis, proposal generation, proposal evaluation, and update implementation (S1--S4), including the recursive application of these stages to improvement mechanisms (RI). We review risks, safeguards, and evaluation evidence for individual updates, effects inherited by successor systems, and revisions to improvement mechanisms, while distinguishing direct RSI findings from evidence in related systems. Finally, we examine evaluation settings, identify requirements for independent and longitudinal assessment, and discuss applications and open research problems.

University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Самосовершенствование AI без потери контроля и доверия
ru.desc: В статье дается определение рекурсивного самосовершенствования (RSI) — процесса, в котором AI-система меняет не только модели, промпты и инструменты, но и собственные механизмы будущих обновлений. Авторы выделяют четыре взаимосвязанных требования к надежному RSI: реальное и устойчивое улучшение, соблюдение поведенческих ограничений, безопасность и приватность, а также прозрачность и управляемость. Анализ строится через три перспективы: валидность улучшений, сохранение ограничений и эффективный надзор над стадиями диагностики, генерации, оценки и внедрения обновлений. Работа также рассматривает риски, передающиеся последующим системам, и необходимость независимой долгосрочной оценки.

en.title: Ensuring Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in AI Systems
en.desc: This paper surveys the concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI systems, focusing on how these systems can enhance themselves through experience and feedback. It outlines the necessary conditions for trustworthy improvements, emphasizing the importance of maintaining behavioral constraints and ensuring system security. The authors propose a framework that categorizes the requirements for effective RSI into four key themes, including improvement validity and transparency. Additionally, the paper discusses the risks associated with self-modification and the need for robust oversight to prevent deterioration of capabilities and compliance issues.

zh.title: 递归自我改进：确保可信的AI进步
zh.desc: 这篇论文调查了递归自我改进（RSI）的概念，并将可信的进步要求组织为改进有效性、约束保持和监督等方面。随着大型模型的不断发展，AI系统越来越依赖经验和反馈来持续改进模型和工作流程。尽管自我修改可以带来改进，但并不保证这些改进是可信的，可能会出现评估缺陷和能力退化等问题。论文提出了RSI的操作定义和过程框架，并从多个角度分析了可信RSI的要求。

papers.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
papers.abstract: Abstract World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls via explicit tokens and interaction-aware positional encoding to improve interactive video generation and navigation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Interactive video world models require coordinated control over viewing perspectives, character actions, and camera motion. Existing methods typically leave view modes implicit in text captions, conflate action with camera motion, and inject controls through fragmented architectural pathways that capture interdependencies only indirectly. In this work, we present World-in-Context, an interactive world modeling framework powered by In-Context Conditioning (ICC). Rather than relying on specialized conditioning pathways, World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls into explicit tokens contextualized directly within a shared self-attention space. Our formulation reveals that (i) explicit view tokens disentangle conflicting dynamics and unlock emergent view switching from single-view data, while (ii) action and camera inputs play complementary roles in governing local responsiveness and global stability. To preserve temporal continuity across execution intervals, we further introduce Interaction-Transport RoPE (IT-RoPE), parameterizing temporal attention with accumulated control transitions. On WBench, World-in-Context-5B achieves navigation performance on par with 22B EchoWM (81.5 vs. 81.6) and attains a 93.8% perspective-switching success rate, substantially outperforming existing 5B baselines (18.8%). Controlled analyses further demonstrate compounding advantages of World-in-Context under richer conditioning mixtures, favorable data efficiency, and natural applicability to causal rollouts.

ru.title: Единый контекст управления делает интерактивные видеомиры управляемыми и согласованными
ru.desc: Авторы представляют World-in-Context — фреймворк для интерактивных world models, который объединяет управление точкой зрения, действиями персонажа и движением камеры через явные токены в общем пространстве self-attention, используя In-Context Conditioning (ICC). Явные view-токены разделяют конфликтующие динамики и позволяют моделировать переключение ракурса даже на данных с одним ракурсом, а действия и камера дополняют друг друга, отвечая за локальную отзывчивость и глобальную стабильность. Для сохранения временной непрерывности предложен IT-RoPE, который параметризует temporal attention накопленными переходами управления. Модель World-in-Context-5B на WBench сопоставима по навигации с 22B EchoWM и достигает 93.8% успешности переключения перспективы против 18.8% у 5B-базовых моделей.

en.title: Unifying Control for Enhanced Interactive Video Generation
en.desc: The paper introduces World-in-Context, a framework designed to enhance interactive video generation by integrating view, action, and camera controls through explicit tokens. This approach addresses limitations in existing methods that often treat these elements separately, leading to inefficiencies in video navigation and generation. By utilizing In-Context Conditioning (ICC) and Interaction-Transport RoPE (IT-RoPE), the framework allows for better coordination and responsiveness in video interactions. The results show significant improvements in navigation performance and perspective-switching success rates compared to previous models, highlighting the effectiveness of unified control mechanisms in interactive video environments.

zh.title: 统一视角与动作的互动视频生成
zh.desc: World-in-Context 是一个交互式世界建模框架，通过显式的标记和交互感知的位置编码，统一了视角、动作和相机控制，从而改善了互动视频生成和导航。该方法通过直接在共享的自注意力空间中上下文化显式视角标记，解决了现有方法中视角模式隐含于文本描述的问题。研究表明，显式视角标记能够解开冲突的动态，并从单视角数据中实现视角切换。同时，动作和相机输入在局部响应性和全局稳定性方面发挥互补作用。

papers.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract MiniTE enables stable low-bit reinforcement learning for large language models by aligning cross-engine numerical execution and accelerating native 4-bit computation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. We show that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient to ensure consistent policy evaluation, highlighting the importance of cross-engine numerical execution. We introduce miniTE, a lightweight framework that combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 (4-bit weights and activations) GEMM computation for LLM RL. It improves numerical execution consistency without modifying the RL objective, while reducing implementation overhead to realize the benefits of native low-bit computation. Long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate stable training and benchmark performance close to BF16, outperforming naive Transformer Engine (TE) NVFP4 in evaluation quality. On single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, yielding 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and TE NVFP4, respectively, for complete learner updates. We released the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training configurations to make native low-bit RL easier.

ru.title: Стабильный RL для LLM в 4 бита: быстрее без потери качества
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают miniTE — лёгкий фреймворк для стабильного обучения с подкреплением (RL) больших языковых моделей (LLM) в низкой битности. Выяснилось, что простого совпадения весов модели и числовых форматов недостаточно: нужна согласованность численного исполнения между отдельными движками обучения и генерации. Метод сочетает диагностику исполнения, численное выравнивание между движками и эффективное нативное W4A4 GEMM-вычисление с 4-битными весами и активациями, не меняя целевую функцию RL. На модели Qwen3-30B-A3B обучение стабильно, качество близко к BF16, а пропускная способность на одном узле NVIDIA B300 выше BF16 в 1.39 раза и TE NVFP4 в 1.47 раза.

en.title: MiniTE: Boosting Low-Bit RL Stability for Large Language Models
en.desc: The paper introduces MiniTE, a framework designed to enhance low-bit reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs). It addresses the challenges of achieving stable learning across different training and sampling engines by emphasizing the need for cross-engine numerical execution. MiniTE combines execution diagnostics and efficient computation methods to improve numerical consistency without altering the RL objectives. The framework demonstrates significant performance improvements in long-horizon RL tasks, achieving higher throughput compared to existing methods while maintaining evaluation quality.

zh.title: MiniTE：稳定的低比特强化学习新框架
zh.desc: MiniTE 是一个轻量级框架，旨在为大型语言模型的低比特强化学习提供稳定性。它通过对跨引擎数值执行的对齐和高效的4位权重与激活计算，改善了数值执行的一致性。研究表明，仅仅匹配模型权重和数值格式不足以确保一致的策略评估，因此跨引擎的数值执行变得尤为重要。通过在 Qwen3-30B-A3B 上进行的长期强化学习实验，MiniTE 显示出比传统方法更高的训练稳定性和评估质量。

papers.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract ProAS improves credit assignment in critic-free reinforcement learning for LLM agents by using a dynamic reference graph to mask unreasonable incentives and redistribute penalties asymmetrically, boosting success rates and convergence speed.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally unreasonable actions in preferred trajectories and ignores each action's downstream deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve fine-grained credit assignment via Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR). Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct demonstrate that ProAS universally elevates mainstream group-based baselines to new state-of-the-art performance, achieving peak success rates of 91.9% and 94.3% on ALFWorld, alongside 66.7% and 70.8% on WebShop, respectively. Furthermore, it accelerates training convergence by up to 2.44times while maintaining strong robustness against imperfect or distilled ARGs. Codes: https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS

ru.title: Справедливая награда для каждого шага LLM-агента
ru.desc: В статье предлагается ProAS — метод улучшения назначения кредита (credit assignment) в критик-free обучении с подкреплением (RL) для LLM-агентов. Существующие алгоритмы вроде GRPO равномерно распределяют преимущество траектории на все действия, что усиливает структурно неразумные действия в успешных траекториях и не учитывает их последствия в неуспешных. ProAS использует динамически обновляемый Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) с техниками маскирования нерациональных стимулов (MUI) и асимметричного перераспределения штрафов (APR). Эксперименты на Qwen2.5 на бенчмарках ALFWorld и WebShop показывают новые state-of-the-art результаты и ускорение сходимости до 2.44 раза.

en.title: Enhancing Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning with ProAS
en.desc: This paper introduces Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a method designed to enhance credit assignment in critic-free reinforcement learning for Large Language Model (LLM) agents. ProAS utilizes a dynamic reference graph to effectively mask unreasonable incentives and redistribute penalties in a way that is not uniform, allowing for more precise credit assignment. By addressing the limitations of existing algorithms that treat all actions equally, ProAS improves the learning process and boosts both success rates and convergence speed. Experimental results show that ProAS significantly outperforms traditional methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance across various benchmarks.

zh.title: ProAS：提升无评论强化学习的信用分配效率
zh.desc: ProAS是一种改进信用分配的框架，专为无评论的强化学习设计，特别适用于大型语言模型（LLM）代理。它通过动态参考图来屏蔽不合理的激励，并不对称地重新分配惩罚，从而提高成功率和收敛速度。研究表明，传统的均匀信用分配方法会强化不合理的行为，而ProAS则通过精细化的信用分配解决了这一问题。实验结果显示，ProAS在多个基准测试中显著提升了性能，并加快了训练过程。

papers.title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
papers.abstract: Abstract Harness self-evolution improves LLM agents via skill adaptation guided by a meta-skill that reformulates guidance to match executor capabilities, boosting weak models without parameter updates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Harness self-evolution offers a practical route for LLM agents to improve from execution experience without updating model parameters. Its effectiveness depends on whether models can successfully act on the guidance provided by their harnesses. However, we find that harness benefits are not uniform across model capabilities: skills that improve stronger models can provide little benefit or even degrade performance for weaker ones. Across seven models and three benchmarks, we identify 103 task-skill pairs where skills improve GPT-5.6-luna by 31.1 points but degrade Gemma-4-E4B by 8.8 points. In 86% of failed weak-model runs, the violated requirement is already stated in the skill. This motivates skill adaptation: reformulating existing skills to match the executor's capabilities and make their guidance easier to execute. To achieve this, we diagnose failures in tool execution, context management, instruction following, and verification, and distill these diagnoses into a fixed meta-skill that guides adaptation during harness self-evolution. Guided by the meta-skill, a capable external rewriter, Kimi-K3, adapts skills without execution evidence, improving the three weak executors by 5.1-14.1 points over the original skills. We then incorporate this adaptation into a five-round self-evolution loop, where each model revises its own skill from execution trajectories and verifier feedback. Across seven executors, from Gemma-4-E4B to Kimi-K2.5, the meta-skill consistently improves final scores by 2.0-5.1 points over the same loop without the meta-skill. Our findings provide practical design guidance for developing more effective harness self-evolution methods.

ru.title: Учим навыки говорить на языке исполнителя, а не наоборот
ru.desc: Авторы показывают, что самоэволюция harness для LLM-агентов работает неравномерно: навыки (skills), которые улучшают сильные модели, могут ухудшать результаты слабых. Чтобы это исправить, предлагается адаптация навыков через фиксированный meta-skill, который переформулирует инструкции под возможности исполнителя без обновления параметров модели. Внешний модель-переписчик адаптирует навыки без execution evidence, а затем включается в цикл самоэволюции из пяти раундов с обратной связью от verifier. Эксперименты на семи моделях и трёх бенчмарках показывают стабильный прирост итоговых метрик на 2.0-5.1 пункта.

en.title: Empowering Weak Models Through Tailored Skill Adaptation
en.desc: This paper introduces a method called harness self-evolution, which helps large language models (LLMs) improve their performance by adapting their skills based on their execution experiences. Instead of changing the model parameters, it uses a meta-skill to reformulate guidance, making it easier for weaker models to follow. The study shows that while stronger models benefit significantly from skill adaptations, weaker models may struggle, sometimes even performing worse. By diagnosing execution failures and using a meta-skill to guide adaptations, the authors demonstrate improvements in performance across various models, highlighting the importance of tailoring skills to match the capabilities of the executor.

zh.title: 自我进化：提升LLM代理的技能适应能力
zh.desc: 本论文提出了一种自我进化的方法，旨在通过技能适应来提升大型语言模型（LLM）代理的性能。该方法利用元技能重新调整指导，使其更符合执行者的能力，从而在不更新模型参数的情况下增强弱模型的表现。研究发现，强模型和弱模型在技能适应上的效果差异显著，某些技能对强模型有益，但对弱模型可能造成负面影响。通过诊断执行失败的原因，论文提出了一种固定的元技能，指导技能的适应过程，从而在多个模型中实现了性能的提升。

papers.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Abstract S3AC introduces a stabilized actor-critic training method with difficulty-aware prompt sampling to improve long reasoning in large language models without relying on grouped rollouts.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. Common alternatives lack token-level credit assignment and typically rely on grouped rollouts to estimate prompt-specific baselines. A critic can address both limitations, but long-CoT critic training is hindered by insufficient coverage of trajectories with diverse lengths and early gradients dominated by the newly initialized value head. We introduce S3AC (Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic) for LLM reasoning, built around a practical critic-training recipe. The trained critic provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines. Using the prompt-level baseline to estimate difficulty, we propose Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS). DAPS combines this estimate with outcome history to select prompts before generation, reducing rollout waste without offline difficulty initialization. S3AC improves group-rollout performance across dense and mixture-of-experts models from 1.5B to 397B parameters, outperforming a modern GRPO variant (GRPO-X). At 35B, it sustains single-rollout training while tested critic-free baselines deteriorate after initial gains.

ru.title: Критик, который учится рассуждать: стабильный обучение LLM без группового сэмплирования
ru.desc: В статье представлен метод S3AC — стабилизированный actor-critic подход для обучения больших языковых моделей (LLM) рассуждениям с помощью reinforcement learning с проверяемыми наградами (RLVR). Авторы предлагают практичный рецепт обучения критика, который даёт токен-уровневые advantage и промпт-специфичные baseline без необходимости групповых rollout. Для отбора сложности промптов вводится Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS), который сокращает расточительную генерацию ещё до rollout. Эксперименты на моделях от 1.5B до 397B параметров показывают превосходство над GRPO-X и стабильную работу даже с одним rollout на масштабе 35B.

en.title: Enhancing Long Reasoning in Language Models with S3AC
en.desc: The paper presents S3AC, a new method for training large language models using a stabilized actor-critic approach that enhances long reasoning capabilities. It introduces Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling (DAPS), which intelligently selects prompts based on their estimated difficulty and past outcomes, minimizing inefficient rollouts. By employing a critic that provides token-specific advantages and prompt-specific baselines, S3AC addresses the challenges of credit assignment and trajectory coverage in reinforcement learning. The results show that S3AC significantly improves performance in various model sizes, particularly in sustaining training effectiveness without relying on traditional critic methods.

zh.title: S3AC：提升长推理的稳定训练方法
zh.desc: S3AC是一种稳定的演员-评论家训练方法，旨在通过难度感知的提示采样来改善大型语言模型的长推理能力，而不依赖于分组回放。该方法避免了在强化学习中进行困难且昂贵的评论家训练，同时解决了缺乏令牌级信用分配的问题。S3AC通过引入实用的评论家训练方案，提供了特定于提示的基线和令牌特定的优势。通过使用提示级基线来估计难度，S3AC有效减少了回放浪费，提升了在不同参数规模模型上的表现。

papers.title: Build, Don't Play: Self-Improving LLM Research Agents Develop a Hearthstone Battlegrounds AI That Rivals Top Players
papers.abstract: Abstract AutoTavern demonstrates that self-improving LLM research agents can autonomously build a faithful game simulator and train a reinforcement learning agent that surpasses top human players in Hearthstone Battlegrounds.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Can LLM agents carry a hard real-world problem from raw data to a system that holds its own against people? We study this in Hearthstone Battlegrounds, an eight-player auto-battler with stochastic shops and battles, hidden information and nearly a thousand interacting cards. We present AutoTavern, a self-improving research system: specialised LLM research agents share a typed research memory, every claim passes verification gates, and live games close the loop, so the agents improve the simulator, opponents and policy and, from the same feedback, their own research process; a human sets goals and rules on ambiguous mechanics. In 20 days AutoTavern built TavernGym, the first faithful, full-content reproduction of the live game, and delivered 23 versions of TavernAgent, trained with PPO against opponents calibrated to real games. TavernAgent plays complete games on the live ladder by itself: its rating rose from 6,000 to about 15,000 and, on the public leaderboard's measure, its last 20 records average a placement of 1.60 with 80% first places, better than the server's ten highest-rated players on every statistic (2.34, 59%). TavernBench, 960 tasks in 40 scenarios, shows that the system the agents built is the strongest player: TavernAgent answers 91% of the play tasks against at most 63% for frontier LLMs, and decides in 0.03 s where they need up to 26 s; within the second a live turn allows, it keeps 90% and no LLM more than 26%. LLM agents build far better than they play. We will open-source TavernBench and TavernGym at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/AutoTavern.

ru.title: LLM-агенты строят игровых чемпионов лучше, чем играют сами
ru.desc: Авторы представляют AutoTavern — систему самоулучшающихся LLM-агентов, которые самостоятельно создают точный симулятор игры Hearthstone Battlegrounds (TavernGym). На его основе обучается агент TavernAgent с помощью reinforcement learning (PPO), который играет на живом сервере. Агент выходит на уровень выше топ-10 игроков по рейтингу и значительно превосходит frontier LLM в тесте TavernBench, принимая решения за 0,03 с. Вывод работы: LLM-агенты лучше справляются с построением систем, чем с непосредственной игрой.

en.title: Self-Improving LLM Agents Dominate Hearthstone Battlegrounds
en.desc: AutoTavern is a system where self-improving large language model (LLM) agents create a game simulator for Hearthstone Battlegrounds and train a reinforcement learning agent called TavernAgent. This agent outperforms top human players by utilizing a specialized research memory and verification gates to enhance its gameplay strategies. Over 20 days, AutoTavern developed a complete replica of the game and trained TavernAgent using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), achieving impressive rankings on the public leaderboard. The system demonstrates that LLM agents can effectively tackle complex real-world problems by iteratively improving their models based on feedback from live gameplay.

zh.title: 自我改进的LLM代理超越人类玩家
zh.desc: AutoTavern展示了自我改进的语言模型（LLM）研究代理能够自主构建一个忠实的游戏模拟器，并训练出一个强化学习代理，其表现超过了顶级人类玩家。该系统在《炉石传说：战场》这一八人自动战斗游戏中进行研究，利用随机商店和战斗、隐藏信息以及近千张互动卡牌。AutoTavern通过共享类型化的研究记忆和验证机制，使得每个声明都经过验证，并通过实时游戏反馈不断改进模拟器和策略。经过20天的开发，AutoTavern成功构建了TavernGym，并训练出23个版本的TavernAgent，其在游戏中的表现优于服务器上排名前十的玩家。

papers.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
