papers.abstract: Abstract OPTIC achieves extreme compression of per-layer embeddings by using token-shared indexed codes and layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path, preserving most model performance at up to 1000x compression with minimal inference overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. We instead develop OPTIC (Output-Path-fitted, Token-shared Indexed Codes), which stores one quantized code tuple per token and decodes it at every layer with a layer-specific affine decoder. Codes and decoders are fitted to the PLE output path rather than to the stored vectors. At about 100times PLE compression of bfloat16 (BF16) E4B, OPTIC retains an aggregate 97.8% of the uncompressed model's performance across seven benchmarks, whereas product quantization, the strongest of six conventional baselines, retains 66.3%. At 594times and 1,002times PLE compression of BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 90.5% and 84.1%. On the official E4B release with 4-bit linear weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16), OPTIC retains 96.9% at about 100times PLE compression. During inference at about 100times PLE compression, BF16 E4B uses 29.7% less GPU memory than with uncompressed PLE at the same key-value cache size, while running at most 0.40% slower.
affiliations: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

ru.title: Сжимаем эмбеддинги в сотни раз, почти не теряя качество LLM
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают метод OPTIC для сильного сжатия Per-Layer Embeddings, которые составляют около 35% параметров модели Gemma 4 E4B. Каждому токену назначается один общий квантованный код, который на каждом слое декодируется отдельным аффинным декодером, обученным под выходной путь модели. При сжатии примерно в 100 раз модель сохраняет 97,8% качества, тогда как product quantization — 66,3%. Метод почти не увеличивает задержку инференса и уменьшает потребление GPU-памяти на 29,7%.

en.title: Extreme Compression with Minimal Performance Loss
en.desc: The paper presents OPTIC, a method for achieving extreme compression of per-layer embeddings in language models, allowing for up to 1000x reduction in size while maintaining high performance. It utilizes token-shared indexed codes and layer-specific affine decoders that are tailored to the output path, which helps preserve model accuracy. Compared to traditional quantization methods, OPTIC significantly outperforms them, retaining up to 97.8% of the original model's performance even at high compression rates. This approach not only reduces memory usage during inference but also minimizes the impact on processing speed, making it a valuable advancement in the field of machine learning.

zh.title: 极致压缩，性能不减
zh.desc: OPTIC是一种极端压缩每层嵌入的方法，通过使用共享的索引编码和特定层的仿射解码器，能够在保持模型性能的同时实现高达1000倍的压缩。该方法针对每个令牌存储一个量化代码元组，并在每一层使用特定的解码器进行解码，从而优化了输出路径。与传统的量化方法相比，OPTIC在594倍和1002倍的压缩下，分别保留了90.5%和84.1%的模型性能。在推理过程中，OPTIC还显著减少了GPU内存的使用，且速度损失极小。

papers.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
papers.abstract: Abstract CausalAlign improves long-horizon camera ego-motion consistency in diffusion video generators by aligning internal representations to 3D dynamics via delta-token space.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.
affiliations: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence

ru.title: CausalAlign: видео, которое не теряет направление камеры
ru.desc: В статье представлен CausalAlign — метод, который улучшает согласованность движения камеры (ego-motion) в диффузионных генераторах видео на длинных временных горизонтах. Авторы с помощью линейных probe-классификаторов и causal interventions диагностируют, как VGM представляют и сохраняют информацию о движении камеры в процессе denoising, и выявляют паттерн «подъёма и спада». Затем внутренние представления выбранных слоёв выравниваются с 3D foundation model через delta-token space, что позволяет фокусироваться на динамике движения, а не на статичном содержимом сцены. После fine-tuning модели Wan2.2 метод повышает точность движения и геометрическую согласованность (более чем на 20%), а также улучшает успешность world action models на задачах мобильной манипуляции в RoboCasa365.

en.title: Enhancing Video Consistency with CausalAlign
en.desc: CausalAlign is a framework designed to enhance the consistency of camera ego-motion in diffusion video generators (VGMs). It addresses the issue of drifting camera motion over long video sequences by aligning internal representations to 3D dynamics using a delta-token space. The framework includes a diagnostic component that analyzes how ego-motion is represented and retained during the video generation process, revealing patterns that can be improved. By aligning these representations to a 3D foundation model, CausalAlign significantly boosts motion accuracy and geometric consistency, leading to better performance in tasks like mobile manipulation.

zh.title: 提升扩散视频生成模型的相机运动一致性
zh.desc: CausalAlign 是一种改进扩散视频生成模型（VGM）中相机自我运动一致性的方法。它通过 delta-token 空间将内部表示与 3D 动态对齐，从而解决了长时间生成视频时相机运动漂移的问题。该框架包含两个部分：首先，通过线性探测和因果干预诊断相机自我运动的表示和使用情况；其次，通过对齐特定层的表示与 3D 基础模型，增强相机自我运动状态。CausalAlign 显著提高了运动准确性、几何一致性和时间平滑性，同时保持了视觉质量。

papers.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
papers.abstract: Abstract EmbodiedLab evaluates embodied agents that must physically interact with simulated laboratory apparatus to discover scientific principles through self-directed experimentation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Embodied agents are expected to accomplish real-world goals by deciding for themselves how and when to interact with their surroundings. For many such goals, changing the physical state of the world is the means rather than the end: the agent changes the state of a system through interaction, observes the feedback, and explores until it either achieves the goal itself (e.g., discovering physical laws) or learns what the goal requires; it acts to know. Manipulation benchmarks stop at acting to change, with the target state given; scientific discovery benchmarks evaluate knowing but replace physical experimentation with symbolic actions or numerical queries. We introduce EmbodiedLab, a benchmark in which a robot must act to know. Quantitative science experiments make this setting controllable: the parameters of the system are resampled for every instance, so the result cannot be known in advance, yet it can be scored exactly. Across 30 experiments in five disciplines on 14 apparatus platforms, the agent receives an objective and the apparatus, chooses its own procedure, and operates a physics-based simulated laboratory, reading the instruments through its cameras. Evaluation checks what the agent came to know, grounded in readings recorded during the episode, as well as the physical state the task requires; every experiment is verified to be solvable. We evaluate six frontier models in their developers' coding agents with native observation and control, with added perception and motion planning, and with manipulation skills distilled from the strongest agents. With native control, even the strongest agent succeeds less than half the time; for every agent, most failures arise in interacting with the apparatus, and manipulation skills help weaker agents more than perception and planning. The benchmark and its evaluation code are available at https://github.com/HexaFuture/EmbodiedLab.

ru.title: Действовать, чтобы узнать: роботы-учёные ещё далеки от успеха
ru.desc: В статье представлен EmbodiedLab — бенчмарк, в котором роботизированные embodied-агенты должны физически взаимодействовать с симулированными лабораторными установками, чтобы открывать научные законы путём самостоятельных экспериментов. Параметры систем случайно перегенерируются для каждого эксперимента, поэтому результат нельзя угадать заранее, но его можно точно оценить. Авторы тестируют шесть передовых моделей (LLM) в агентных средах с нативным управлением, а также с добавлением восприятия и планирования движения и с навыками манипуляции. Даже лучший агент справляется менее чем в половине случаев, а большинство ошибок связано с взаимодействием с установкой.

en.title: Empowering Agents to Discover Through Interaction
en.desc: EmbodiedLab is a new benchmark designed for embodied agents that learn scientific principles through physical interaction with simulated laboratory equipment. These agents must decide how and when to manipulate their environment to achieve real-world goals, focusing on exploration and feedback rather than just reaching a predetermined target state. The benchmark includes 30 experiments across five scientific disciplines, where agents must autonomously determine their procedures and operate within a physics-based simulation. Evaluation is based on the knowledge gained by the agent and the physical state required for task completion, highlighting the importance of manipulation skills in achieving success.

zh.title: 通过行动获取知识的智能体实验
zh.desc: EmbodiedLab 是一个评估具身智能体的基准，智能体需要与模拟实验室设备进行物理互动，以通过自我导向的实验发现科学原理。智能体通过改变系统的物理状态来实现目标，并观察反馈，探索直到达到目标或学习所需的条件。与传统的操作基准不同，EmbodiedLab 强调智能体在实验中必须通过行动来获取知识，而不仅仅是执行给定的操作。该基准涵盖了多个学科的实验，评估智能体在真实环境中的表现和学习能力。

papers.title: Rethinking Video Storage for AI Training: Breaking Cross-Frame Dependencies for Efficient Random Access
papers.abstract: Abstract Co-designed sparse decoding and dependency-decoupled encoding reduce video decode overhead for random AI training sampling by bounding reconstruction per target.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. However, existing video storage paradigms are optimized for sequential playback and employ sophisticated inter-frame reference structures to maximize compression efficiency. When applied to the random-sampling workloads of AI training, these paradigms face substantial decoding-efficiency bottlenecks. Workarounds such as independent JPEG frames and short groups of pictures (GOPs) reduce decoding work at the cost of larger storage and transfer volumes. In this paper, we identify two sources of decode amplification: sequential reconstruction of unrelated frames and reconstruction of the reference chains required by sampled targets. We address both sources by co-designing the decoding schedule and video reference structure. Dependency-aware sparse decoding reconstructs only requested frames and their required references, skipping unrelated reconstruction without transcoding the source videos. Optional offline Dependency-Decoupled Random Access (DDRA) encoding further reduces reference reconstruction by restricting each interior frame to two bounding intra-coded anchors. Together, sparse decoding and DDRA retain inter-frame prediction while bounding reconstruction to at most three frames per requested target, independent of the intra period. Experiments on a large-scale robotics corpus show that, at comparable reconstruction quality, our method achieves 1.45times the loading throughput of LeRobot v3 with 58.7% less media payload.

ru.title: Декодируем только нужные кадры — быстрее обучение без потери качества
ru.desc: Статья посвящена ускорению декодирования видео при случайной выборке кадров, которая типична для обучения крупных AI-моделей. Авторы выделяют две причины избыточного декодирования: последовательную реконструкцию ненужных кадров и восстановление цепочек опорных кадров (reference chains) для целевых кадров. Предложены разреженное декодирование с учётом зависимостей (dependency-aware sparse decoding) и опциональное офлайн-кодирование DDRA, которое ограничивает опорные кадры двумя intra-кодированными якорями, так что на каждый запрошенный кадр реконструируется не более трёх кадров. На крупном робототехническом датасете метод даёт в 1.45 раза большую пропускную способность загрузки, чем LeRobot v3, при 58.7% меньшем объёме медиаданных.

en.title: Efficient Video Decoding for AI Training with Sparse and Decoupled Techniques
en.desc: This paper presents a novel approach to improve video decoding efficiency for AI training that uses random sampling. It introduces co-designed sparse decoding and dependency-decoupled encoding to minimize the overhead associated with reconstructing video frames. By focusing only on the frames that are needed and their necessary references, the method avoids unnecessary decoding of unrelated frames. The results demonstrate significant improvements in loading throughput while reducing the amount of data that needs to be stored and transferred.

zh.title: 优化视频解码，提高AI训练效率
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种联合设计的稀疏解码和依赖解耦编码方法，以减少随机AI训练采样中的视频解码开销。传统的视频存储方式优化了顺序播放，但在随机采样的AI训练中面临解码效率瓶颈。我们通过优化解码调度和视频参考结构，解决了解码放大问题，仅重建所需帧及其参考，而跳过无关帧的重建。实验结果表明，该方法在保持相似重建质量的同时，加载吞吐量提高了1.45倍，媒体负载减少了58.7%。

papers.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
papers.abstract: Abstract RynnVLA-Latent leverages latent actions derived from diverse video to pretrain large vision-language-action policies, achieving high success across simulated and real-world robot benchmarks without embodiment-specific tuning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. We present RynnVLA-Latent, a framework that turns heterogeneous interaction videos into scalable supervision for robot policy pretraining. At its core, RynnLAM learns continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions from visual transitions without requiring native robot controls. By combining residual future-feature prediction, camera-compensated 3D-flow supervision, and camera-motion decoupling, RynnLAM encourages representations that capture control-relevant motion rather than appearance changes alone. We apply RynnLAM to 30.1K hours of human, robot, and simulation videos, producing 745.52M latent-action descriptors. RynnVLA-Latent then learns to predict latent-action chunks from visual observations and language through flow matching, before adapting its pretrained backbone and action expert to embodiment-specific robot actions. The resulting 4B policy achieves 98.8% success on LIBERO, 84.7% on LIBERO-Plus without benchmark-specific adaptation, 51.9% average success across five VLABench tracks, and 88.6% average success on the RoboTwin 2.0 bimanual benchmark. It also achieves the highest observed success rates among the compared methods on six real-world manipulation tasks across dexterous-hand and mobile-gripper platforms. Together with representation ablations and data-scaling results, these findings demonstrate the potential of latent-action supervision for scaling robot policy learning beyond native action-labeled data.

ru.title: Учим роботов действовать по видео без размеченных действий
ru.desc: Авторы представляют RynnVLA-Latent — фреймворк, который использует видео с людьми, роботами и симуляций для предобучения vision-language-action политик. Ключевой компонент RynnLAM учится извлекать непрерывные 3D-осведомлённые latent actions из визуальных переходов без доступа к нативным управляющим сигналам робота. Модель предсказывает цепочки latent actions по визуальным наблюдениям и языку с помощью flow matching, а затем адаптируется к конкретному роботу. Итоговая модель на 4B параметров показывает высокие результаты на LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, VLABench и RoboTwin 2.0, а также на реальных задачах манипуляции, что демонстрирует потенциал масштабирования обучения роботов за пределы размеченных данных.

en.title: Unlocking Robot Learning with Latent Actions
en.desc: RynnVLA-Latent is a framework that enhances robot learning by using latent actions extracted from various videos, allowing for effective pretraining of vision-language-action policies. It addresses the challenge of limited action-labeled data and differing control systems in robots by generating scalable supervision from heterogeneous interaction videos. The core innovation involves learning continuous, 3D-grounded latent actions that focus on relevant motion rather than just visual appearance. This approach has led to impressive success rates in both simulated and real-world robot tasks, showcasing the effectiveness of latent-action supervision in advancing robot policy learning.

zh.title: 潜在动作监督：机器人策略学习的新突破
zh.desc: RynnVLA-Latent 是一种利用多样视频中提取的潜在动作来预训练大型视觉-语言-动作策略的框架。它能够在模拟和真实世界的机器人基准测试中取得高成功率，而无需针对特定机器人进行调优。该框架通过从视觉转变中学习连续的三维潜在动作，结合未来特征预测和相机运动解耦，鼓励捕捉与控制相关的运动。最终，RynnVLA-Latent 在多个基准测试中表现出色，展示了潜在动作监督在机器人策略学习中的巨大潜力。

papers.title: More Memory, Better Videos? A Controlled Study of Visual Memory in Long-Video Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Visual memory improves historical consistency but can reduce current-story accuracy by reinforcing outdated appearances, showing that retrieval relevance alone does not prove memory utility.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-video generators increasingly retrieve past visual observations to prevent identity drift. The intuition is compelling: more access to history should make future video more consistent. But an image can be faithful to the past and wrong for the present. Does visual memory always improve the generated story? We investigate this question through VMem-Bench, a two-track diagnostic study. Track-A measures which references are selected from 92 real films (16,548 segments), before generation and without generator confounds. Track-B compares four retrieval policies with no-memory and gold-informed last-seen controls on 30 causally generated stories (2,824 segments) using a shared generator. Retrieval increases entity recall from 0.559 to 0.628-0.693 and improves similarity to past appearances, but decreases precision from 0.977 to 0.915-0.938 and forbidden-entity avoidance from 0.968 to 0.845-0.898. It can also reinforce obsolete appearances after the story changes them. Conversely, high long-gap recall can arise without memory when the prompt itself supplies the appearance; an appearance-stripping analysis exposes this confound. These results distinguish historical fidelity from current-story correctness and show why retrieval relevance or final-video consistency alone does not establish memory utility.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Верность прошлому не равна правильности настоящего
ru.desc: Авторы исследуют, всегда ли визуальная память улучшает генерацию длинных видео с LLM-подобными генераторами, которые извлекают прошлые кадры, чтобы не терять идентичность персонажей. Используется бенчмарк VMem-Bench с двумя треками: отбор референсов на 92 реальных фильмах и сравнение политик извлечения на сгенерированных историях. Результаты показывают, что память повышает полноту сущностей и похожесть на прошлые образы, но снижает точность и избегание запрещённых сущностей, а иногда закрепляет устаревшую внешность. Вывод: релевантность извлечения и согласованность видео сами по себе не доказывают полезность памяти для текущего сюжета.

en.title: Balancing Memory and Accuracy in Video Generation
en.desc: This paper explores how visual memory affects the consistency and accuracy of generated stories in long-video generation. It introduces VMem-Bench, a diagnostic study that evaluates the impact of memory retrieval on story generation through two tracks: one measuring reference selection from real films and the other comparing different retrieval policies. The findings reveal that while retrieval can enhance recall of entities and maintain historical fidelity, it may also lead to decreased precision and reinforce outdated appearances. Ultimately, the study highlights that memory utility cannot be determined solely by retrieval relevance or consistency with past visuals, as current-story accuracy is equally important.

zh.title: 视觉记忆：历史一致性与当前准确性的权衡
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了视觉记忆在生成视频故事中的作用。研究发现，虽然视觉记忆可以提高历史一致性，但可能会降低当前故事的准确性。通过VMem-Bench的两轨诊断研究，作者比较了不同的检索策略，发现检索可以提高实体回忆率，但同时降低了精确度。最终，研究表明，仅凭检索相关性或最终视频一致性并不能证明记忆的有效性。

papers.title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Thinking-in-Bets improves agent reliability by having models record verified claims before receiving user feedback, reducing false reversals and unnecessary edits while maintaining accuracy.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Language model agents often abandon correct work when a user challenges it, yet simply telling them to stand firm makes them ignore real mistakes. Once an agent reads a complaint, it tends to discount its own earlier checks in order to agree with the user. We introduce Thinking-in-Bets, a training-free method in which an agent writes a short private record of its main claims, the checks supporting them, and its confidence before reading user feedback. When challenged, the agent consults this Claim Checklist to keep verified work intact while investigating uncertain or newly challenged parts. We evaluate five Gemini models (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash, and 4.0 Argon) across eight benchmarks: SWE-Together, SWE-Interact, and DeepSWE for software engineering, Agents' Last Exam for professional reports, Humanity's Last Exam and SycEval for academic reasoning, Vals Finance for financial analysis, and Terminal-Bench for command-line tasks. Recording claims before criticism nearly eliminates false reversals in patch review and protects passing report drafts under mistaken pushback, whereas writing the same record after reading the complaint recovers very little of the gain. In multi-turn coding, pre-reply claim records substantially reduce unnecessary file edits after mistaken complaints, and gating the record so it is written only when the agent is uncertain lowers token overhead while fixing more real bugs than the baseline. Even in non-interactive tasks without user feedback, listing the key claims in a draft and re-checking the weakest one before submission improves both answer accuracy and confidence estimates across all tested models.

ru.title: Фиксируй утверждения до критики, а не после
ru.desc: Статья предлагает метод Thinking-in-Bets, не требующий дополнительного обучения: перед тем как получить обратную связь от пользователя, LLM-агент записывает свои ключевые утверждения, подтверждающие проверки и уровень уверенности. При критике агент опирается на этот Claim Checklist, что предотвращает ложные отказы от верных решений и лишние правки. Эксперименты на пяти моделях Gemini и восьми бенчмарках (SWE-Together, DeepSWE, Humanity's Last Exam, Terminal-Bench и других) показывают почти полное устранение ложных откатов. Даже без обратной связи перепроверка самого слабого утверждения перед ответом повышает точность и качество оценки уверенности.

en.title: Enhancing Agent Reliability with Thinking-in-Bets
en.desc: The paper introduces a method called Thinking-in-Bets, which enhances the reliability of machine learning agents by having them document their verified claims before receiving user feedback. This approach helps prevent agents from abandoning correct outputs when faced with user challenges, as they can refer back to their recorded claims instead of immediately conceding to user input. The study evaluates multiple Gemini models across various benchmarks, demonstrating that pre-recording claims significantly reduces false reversals and unnecessary edits in response to user complaints. Overall, this method not only maintains accuracy but also boosts the agents' confidence in their outputs, even in non-interactive scenarios.

zh.title: 提升智能体可靠性的思维方式
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为“Thinking-in-Bets”的方法，旨在提高智能体的可靠性。该方法要求模型在接收用户反馈之前，记录经过验证的主张及其支持证据，从而减少错误反转和不必要的编辑。通过这种方式，智能体在面对用户质疑时，可以参考自己的主张清单，保持已验证工作的完整性。研究表明，这种方法在多个基准测试中显著提高了模型的准确性和信心估计。

papers.title: AgentProofBench: Benchmarking Reusable Verifiers for Web Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract AgentProofBench evaluates reusable web-agent verification by linking frozen acceptance rules to execution traces, establishing baseline measurements for program-gate correctness and reuse.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reusable Web-agent verification requires a rule to follow changing requirements and support subsequent execution. We introduce AgentProofBench, which connects paired tests of a frozen acceptance rule to execution from identical saved openings. The resource spans 97 tasks, 79 families, and four Web services. Experiments with DeepSeek Flash/Pro establish two linked measurements. Across 48 families, complete-panel and decision-replay tests retain 82/96 Flash and 79/96 Pro source programs; paired reuse-rebuild BA intervals are [-5.47, 1.57] and [-10.16, 0.00] percentage points. Across 22 execution families, deployment-state panel correctness separates program assignments whose two saved openings are both delivered correctly: 32/33 assignments with error-free panels, versus 1/11 with panel errors. All reference-defined program-gate regressions and withheld deliveries occur in the latter group. Neutral continuation attains the highest correct delivery under the tested generic feedback, providing a concrete baseline for measuring the value added by a gate. Released instructions, states, programs, reference rules, and trajectories connect each test failure to its execution consequences. AgentProofBench makes reusable verification assessable at both the requirement and policy levels.
affiliations: School of Computer Science, Carnegie Mellon University

ru.title: Проверяем не только код, но и правила: AgentProofBench делает верификацию web-агентов измеримой
ru.desc: Статья представляет AgentProofBench — бенчмарк для оценки переиспользуемой верификации web-агентов, связывающий замороженные правила приёмки с трассами выполнения. Набор включает 97 задач, 79 семейств и четыре web-сервиса, а эксперименты с моделями DeepSeek Flash и Pro задают базовые измерения корректности program-gate и переиспользования. Показано, что наличие ошибок на панели тестов сильно связано с регрессиями и недоставкой результатов, тогда как нейтральное продолжение даёт наибольшую корректную доставку и служит baseline для оценки пользы gate. Выпущенные инструкции, состояния, программы, эталонные правила и траектории позволяют связать каждый провал теста с его последствиями при исполнении.

en.title: Enhancing Reusable Web-Agent Verification with AgentProofBench
en.desc: AgentProofBench is a framework designed to evaluate the verification of reusable web agents by linking acceptance rules to their execution traces. It establishes baseline measurements for correctness and reuse of programs across various tasks and web services. The framework allows for testing the adaptability of rules to changing requirements while ensuring that execution remains consistent. By providing concrete metrics for program-gate correctness, AgentProofBench enhances the assessment of verification processes at both requirement and policy levels.

zh.title: AgentProofBench：可重用网络代理验证的新基准
zh.desc: AgentProofBench 是一个用于评估可重用网络代理验证的工具，它通过将冻结的接受规则与执行轨迹相连接，建立了程序门正确性和重用的基准测量。该工具支持在不断变化的需求下进行规则的遵循和后续执行。实验结果显示，在多个任务和网络服务中，AgentProofBench 能够有效地连接测试与执行，提供准确的测量指标。通过对执行状态面板的正确性分析，AgentProofBench 使得可重用验证在需求和政策层面上都变得可评估。

papers.title: Novel or Not? PatEx-Gym: Agentic Prior-Art Search for Novelty Assessment in Patent Examination
papers.abstract: Abstract PatEx-Gym introduces a framework with benchmarks, synthetic trajectory data, and a compact agent to evaluate iterative prior-art search and patent examination.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Patent examination is a challenging real-world task that requires agents to discover sparse prior art, iteratively refine queries, inspect technical evidence, and produce novelty assessments documented in Office Actions (OAs) across heterogeneous scientific and technical domains. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on static and limited candidate sets, leaving the full search--reasoning--assessment process underexplored. We present PatEx-Gym, the first framework for developing and evaluating agents for patent examination, which integrates three components. First, PatEx-Bench provides 1K realistic examination tasks, two large-scale retrieval corpora containing over 1M patents and 52K scientific papers, and a harness runtime supporting iterative search, document visits, reasoning, and OA generation. Second, we introduce PASS, an annotation-free Prior-Art Agentic Search Trajectory Synthesis framework. Specifically, it exploits document visits as implicit relevance signals and evidence-acquisition anchors to model intra-turn query behavior, inter-turn search progression, and trajectory-level evidence and outcome quality, yielding PatEx-SynData. Third, we train PatEx-Agent at the 4B scale via supervised fine-tuning on the curated trajectories, establishing a lightweight baseline. Extensive experiments show that final decision accuracy alone does not fully reflect examination quality, while prior-art discovery remains difficult even for strong frontier models. Our PatEx-Agent achieves competitive performance against substantially larger general-purpose agents. These results show that training on PatEx-SynData enables a compact 4B model to serve as a competitive baseline for prior-art search and patent examination. We view patent examination as a demanding testbed for agentic search and deep research agents.
affiliations: Shenzhen Institute of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Маленький агент на синтетических траекториях поиска конкурирует с большими моделями в патентной экспертизе
ru.desc: Статья представляет PatEx-Gym — фреймворк для обучения и оценки LLM-агентов, которые проводят поиск патентного прототипа (prior art) и экспертизу патентов. Авторы создали PatEx-Bench с 1000 задачами и двумя крупными корпусами: более 1 млн патентов и 52 тыс. научных статей, а также метод PASS для автоматической синтетической генерации траекторий поиска без ручной разметки, используя посещения документов как неявные сигналы релевантности. На основе этих данных обучена компактная модель PatEx-Agent размером 4B с помощью supervised fine-tuning. Результаты показывают, что она конкурирует с значительно более крупными универсальными агентами, а сама задача патентной экспертизы является сложным полигоном для агентного поиска и deep research агентов.

en.title: Revolutionizing Patent Examination with PatEx-Gym
en.desc: PatEx-Gym is a new framework designed to improve the process of patent examination by providing benchmarks and synthetic data for evaluating search agents. It includes realistic tasks and large datasets of patents and scientific papers to help agents learn how to find relevant prior art and assess novelty. The framework introduces a novel synthesis method that uses document interactions as signals to guide the search process and improve the quality of evidence gathered. By training a compact 4 billion parameter model, PatEx-Agent, on this data, the study demonstrates that smaller models can perform competitively in complex patent examination tasks.

zh.title: 专利审查的新框架：PatEx-Gym
zh.desc: PatEx-Gym是一个用于评估专利审查的框架，提供基准测试、合成轨迹数据和紧凑型代理。它解决了现有基准主要集中在静态候选集的问题，探索了完整的搜索、推理和评估过程。该框架包括三个部分：PatEx-Bench提供了1000个真实的审查任务和超过100万个专利的检索语料库。通过训练PatEx-Agent，我们展示了一个紧凑的4B模型在专利搜索和审查中的竞争力。

papers.title: ReGE: Stronger Agents through Experience Synthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract ReGE converts recorded agent execution experience into synthesized guidance to improve subsequent task attempts without requiring stronger teachers or parameter updates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Repeated attempts at interactive tasks uncover facts, useful operations, and failures that can inform subsequent execution. We introduce ReGE, a framework for turning this recorded experience into guidance for a fresh attempt. Its main implementation, ReGE-Syn, uses a single coach call to jointly synthesize bounded execution records and available artifacts into self-contained guidance, connecting task-specific findings with proposed actions and relevant pitfalls. A student starts from the task's initial environment state and adapts this guidance to current observations. Source generation, synthesis, and student execution use the same base model, without parameter updates or a stronger teacher. Across four benchmarks, ReGE improves accuracy by an average of 9.9 percentage points for GPT and 8.8 percentage points for Claude compared with unguided execution. On matched BrowseComp-Plus subsets, ReGE-Syn reduces guidance-construction tokens by 98.2\% on GPT and 95.5\% on Claude relative to adapted AggAgent, with observed success. Combined construction and execution tokens decrease by 15.7\% and 35.4\%, respectively, counting input plus output and excluding source generation. BrowseComp-Plus ablations further associate access to process information with fewer student steps and show that joint synthesis produces substantially shorter guidance than Direct history or Independent summaries, with observed success. These results demonstrate how agents can use their own recorded experience to improve subsequent task completion, and suggest a low-cost way to consolidate the execution records of parallel agent systems such as agent swarms.
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

ru.title: Опыт агента — в подсказки для следующей попытки без дообучения
ru.desc: Статья представляет ReGE — фреймворк, который превращает записанный опыт выполнения агента в структурированные рекомендации для последующих попыток без дообучения параметров и без более сильного учителя. Основная реализация ReGE-Syn использует один вызов coach-модели, чтобы совместно синтезировать ограниченные логи выполнения и доступные артефакты в самодостаточные инструкции с действиями и подводными камнями. Студент, начиная с исходного состояния среды, адаптирует эти рекомендации к текущим наблюдениям, при этом все этапы используют одну базовую LLM. На четырёх бенчмарках ReGE повышает точность в среднем на 9.9 п.п. для GPT и 8.8 п.п. для Claude, при этом значительно сокращая токены на построение рекомендаций.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Self-Learned Guidance
en.desc: The paper introduces ReGE, a framework that transforms recorded experiences of agents into synthesized guidance for improving future task attempts. This approach allows agents to learn from their past executions without needing stronger teachers or changing their parameters. The main implementation, ReGE-Syn, efficiently combines execution records and relevant artifacts to create actionable guidance for new attempts. The results show significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating how agents can leverage their own experiences to enhance performance in interactive tasks.

zh.title: 利用经验提升任务执行的智能框架
zh.desc: ReGE是一种将记录的代理执行经验转化为合成指导的框架，旨在改善后续任务尝试。它通过分析重复的交互任务，提取有用的信息和操作，从而为新的执行提供指导。ReGE-Syn是其主要实现，通过一次教练调用，将执行记录和可用文档合成自包含的指导，帮助学生适应当前的观察。实验结果表明，ReGE显著提高了模型的准确性，并减少了指导构建所需的令牌数量，展示了代理如何利用自身经验来提升任务完成率。

papers.title: Nested Sparsity for Scalable Pretraining and Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Nestor introduces nested sparsity in attention to improve conditional computation over standard mixture-of-experts transformers, enhancing pretraining, long-context adaptation, and continual learning.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, the standard backbone for modern large-scale deep learning, employ conditional computation: only a sparse subset of model weights is used in each forward pass. In MoE transformers, this sparsity arises in the MoE operator, which generalizes the multi-layer perceptron in the classical transformer. In this work, we explore an alternative mechanism for conditional computation that analogously generalizes the attention operator. The sparsity induced by this mechanism naturally nests (i.e., hierarchically composes) with the sparsity induced by the MoE operator. We show that a transformer employing this nested sparsity mechanism, which we call Nestor, performs better than a conventional MoE transformer at equal compute and equal sparsity in language model pretraining. We also show that Nestor is well-suited for continual pretraining: it can be adapted to longer contexts more effectively than conventional MoEs, as well as adapt more efficiently to new domains while forgetting less on old domains. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits persist as model size, dataset size, and context length grow. Our results demonstrate the potential of alternative conditional computation mechanisms for deep neural network architectures. Code and checkpoints are available on GitHub at https://github.com/Ma-Lab-Berkeley/Nestor .

ru.title: Вложенная разреженность внимания делает трансформеры умнее и гибче
ru.desc: Статья представляет Nestor — новую архитектуру трансформера, в которой условные вычисления реализуются через вложенную разреженность внимания (nested sparsity in attention). Этот механизм обобщает оператор attention аналогично тому, как MoE обобщает MLP, и естественно комбинируется с разреженностью MoE-слоёв. В экспериментах Nestor превосходит обычный MoE-трансформер при равных вычислительных затратах и уровне разреженности в pretraining языковых моделей. Кроме того, модель эффективнее адаптируется к более длинным контекстам и новым доменам, при этом меньше забывая старые данные (catastrophic forgetting), и эти преимущества сохраняются при масштабировании.

en.title: Nestor: Nested Sparsity for Enhanced Transformer Performance
en.desc: This paper introduces Nestor, a new approach that enhances attention mechanisms in transformers by incorporating nested sparsity. Unlike traditional mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers, which use a sparse selection of weights, Nestor allows for a hierarchical composition of sparsity that improves conditional computation. The authors demonstrate that Nestor outperforms standard MoE transformers in language model pretraining while maintaining the same computational resources. Additionally, Nestor shows superior adaptability for longer contexts and continual learning, making it a promising alternative for future deep learning architectures.

zh.title: Nestor：嵌套稀疏性提升变换器性能
zh.desc: Nestor引入了嵌套稀疏性在注意力机制中，以改善标准混合专家变换器的条件计算。通过这种机制，模型在每次前向传播中只使用稀疏的权重，从而提高了预训练、长上下文适应和持续学习的效果。Nestor的嵌套稀疏性与传统的混合专家操作符的稀疏性自然结合，使得在相同计算和稀疏度下，Nestor在语言模型预训练中表现优于传统的混合专家变换器。我们的研究表明，Nestor在适应新领域时效率更高，同时对旧领域的遗忘更少，且这些优势在模型规模、数据集规模和上下文长度增加时依然存在。

papers.title: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract The study introduces iPrefBench, a benchmark for assessing whether mobile agents can infer missing user preferences from activity history or ask for necessary clarification, revealing that current agents execute actions well but fail at personalization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small An agent that truly knows and acts on behalf of its user has been a long-standing promise of AI assistants. Computer-use agents bring this promise within reach by capably executing fully specified tasks across apps. However, real-world user requests are often underspecified. To act correctly for the particular user, an agent must infer some missing information from the user's activity history and ask for other information that only the user can provide, without making unsupported assumptions or burdening the user with unnecessary questions. We present iPrefBench, a benchmark for evaluating the infer and ask capabilities of personal mobile-use agents in an executable iOS environment with an interactive simulated user. Grounded in a coherent persona with 3,051 past activity events, iPrefBench comprises 130 underspecified user tasks across 26 apps. Each omitted user-dependent requirement is, by construction, either history-inferable or ask-only. iPrefBench evaluates personalized mobile agents on both whether agents complete tasks correctly for the user (i.e., personalized task completion) and whether they seek user input when necessary (i.e., user-agent interaction). Evaluation of 7 frontier agents reveals a substantial gap between execution and personalization. Agents achieve high action completion scores (up to 91.6%) but low full task success (up to 47.7%) because personalization lags behind. They especially struggle with ask-only information, failing to request enough necessary information. Our findings highlight a challenge for personalized agents in knowing what to infer and when to ask. We hope that iPrefBench can serve as a valuable testbed for building agents that know their user and work with them.

ru.title: Агент должен знать, когда догадаться, а когда спросить
ru.desc: Статья представляет iPrefBench — бенчмарк для оценки мобильных агентов на базе LLM, которые должны выводить недостающие предпочтения пользователя из истории его активности или задавать уточняющие вопросы. Тестирование проходит в исполняемой среде iOS с интерактивным симулированным пользователем и 130 недоопределёнными задачами в 26 приложениях. Оценка семи современных агентов показала, что они хорошо выполняют отдельные действия (до 91,6%), но редко полностью решают задачу (до 47,7%), особенно плохо запрашивая информацию, которую может дать только пользователь. Работа показывает, что главная сложность персонализации — понять, что можно вывести самостоятельно, а когда нужно спросить.

en.title: Bridging the Gap: Enhancing Personalization in Mobile Agents
en.desc: The paper presents iPrefBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate mobile agents' ability to infer missing user preferences from their activity history or to ask for necessary clarifications. It highlights that while current agents can execute tasks effectively, they often fall short in personalizing their actions based on individual user needs. The benchmark includes a simulated user environment with a rich history of activities and tasks that are either inferable or require user input. The study reveals a significant gap between task execution and personalization, emphasizing the need for agents to improve their ability to ask for information when required.

zh.title: 个性化代理的挑战：推断与请求的平衡
zh.desc: 本研究介绍了iPrefBench，这是一个用于评估移动代理从活动历史中推断缺失用户偏好或请求必要澄清能力的基准。当前的代理在执行任务方面表现良好，但在个性化方面存在不足。iPrefBench通过模拟用户的交互环境，评估代理在完成用户任务时的个性化能力和用户交互能力。研究发现，尽管代理的任务完成率很高，但个性化成功率较低，尤其在请求用户信息方面表现不佳。

papers.title: Joint or Per-Option? Compact Encoders for Closed-Set Decisions from 17 Million to 1 Billion Parameters
papers.abstract: Abstract  Many language-model pipelines end in a closed-set decision, such as selecting a tool. Prompting a large language model for it is slow and order-sensitive. We ask how small an encoder for such decisions can be and whether it should read the options jointly or separately. In a three-seed study at 32 million parameters, per-option scoring beats joint scoring on a held-out sample of a 37-benchmark decision suite by 5.8 points of chance-corrected skill at matched optimizer steps and by 2.8 at approximately matched training compute; two external benchmarks agree, though not significantly on their unseen tasks. Crossing reader with initialisation shows that the advantage requires a reranker initialisation, whose query-candidate pair input matches per-option reading; from the raw encoder the two readers are indistinguishable. Per-option scoring needs 5 to 13 times more encoder passes: at most twice the median latency, but more than four times the mean. Of six released joint encoders (17 million to 1 billion parameters), the 68- and 150-million-parameter models exceed a 435-million-parameter DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot classifier by 4.9 and 5.9 accuracy points on 209 overlap-audited System1-Arena tasks and are at least on par with it on the 145 tasks unseen in training. The smallest answers a median request in 14 milliseconds on 16 processor threads, against 728 for the classifier. Reordering options changes 12 to 23% of the joint models' answers (per-option scoring: none). Up to 68 million parameters, they lead their size range on a public leaderboard's private, mainly in-distribution tests.

ru.title: Маленький энкодер быстрее и надёжнее LLM для выбора инструмента
ru.desc: Авторы исследуют, насколько маленьким может быть энкодер для задач выбора из закрытого набора вариантов, например выбора инструмента, вместо медленного промптинга LLM. Сравниваются два подхода: совместное чтение всех вариантов (joint scoring) и оценка каждого варианта отдельно (per-option scoring), причём преимущество per-option подхода проявляется при инициализации reranker-моделью. Модели с 68 и 150 миллионами параметров превосходят zero-shot классификатор на базе DeBERTa-v3 на 435 миллионов параметров по точности и при этом отвечают за миллисекунды. Совместные модели чувствительны к порядку вариантов и меняют 12–23% ответов при перестановке, тогда как per-option оценка устойчива к этому.

en.title: Smaller Encoders, Smarter Decisions!
en.desc: This paper investigates the efficiency of small encoders in language model pipelines for decision-making tasks. It compares two scoring methods: per-option scoring, which evaluates options separately, and joint scoring, which assesses them together. The results show that per-option scoring outperforms joint scoring in terms of accuracy, despite requiring more processing passes. Additionally, the study highlights that smaller models can achieve competitive performance while maintaining lower latency compared to larger classifiers.

zh.title: 小型编码器在决策任务中的优势
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了语言模型在决策任务中的表现，特别是如何选择工具。研究发现，逐项评分的方式在多个基准测试中优于联合评分，尽管逐项评分需要更多的编码器传递。作者还指出，使用重新排序的初始化可以提高逐项评分的效果。最终，研究表明小型编码器在处理速度和准确性上具有竞争力，尤其是在特定的任务上。

papers.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Can Small Open-Weight Models Get Real Coding Work Done?
papers.abstract: Abstract Empirical studies of open-weight coding agents reveal that verified code success depends on serving setup, protocol design, and hidden behavioral checks rather than text coherence alone.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Making an open-weight language model generate text is not the same as making it finish coding work. This retrospective empirical systems experience report follows my engineering work from July to October 2026 across coding clients, model-specific serving recipes, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and MLX. Models behind a nominally compatible endpoint still differed in tool-call formatting, turn control, context behavior, cache reuse, and reliability. A served model, coherent text, executed tool calls, and code that passes independent behavioral checks proved to be distinct levels of progress. The evidence includes 4,165 coding-agent gateway turns from my own sessions, 623 debug jobs, and three separate delegation studies with hidden behavioral checks and a fixed Claude Opus 5.5 parent. Saved cold-prefix requests had a median time to first token of about 69.4 s, versus 2.8 s for high-reuse requests (observational). In a 45-trial study, direct coding passed 15/15 and delegation to a quantized Qwen3-Coder 30B-A3B worker passed 12/15 and 14/15. On a second 15-task suite under a fixed artifact contract, the completed replacement cohort had 45/45 for direct coding and 12/45 for a Nemotron Cascade 2 worker (11 worker substitutions). Sixteen sessions stopped by a subscription limit before any model call were replaced; counting them as failures gives 37/45 and 8/45. A Qwen3-Coder worker passed 0/45. In both studies with a direct arm, direct coding had lower API list-price-equivalent frontier cost per verified success. A post-hoc diagnostic found that 19 of 36 artifacts rejected only for renamed parameters passed the hidden checks unchanged; they are not counted as successes.   The contribution is an evidence-qualified account of serving, agent protocol, session continuity, artifact validation, and verification in practice. The studies are not pooled and do not rank models or runtimes.

ru.title: Текст — не код: успех агента решают serving, протокол и проверки
ru.desc: Статья показывает, что успешность open-weight LLM-агентов в задачах программирования зависит не только от связности текста, но и от настроек serving (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, MLX), протокола вызова инструментов и скрытых поведенческих тестов. Авторы сравнивают прямое написание кода с делегированием части работы более слабому worker-модели на 45-trial и 15-задачных наборах данных. Результаты показывают, что прямой подход чаще проходит проверки и дешевле в пересчёте на верифицированный успех, а разные уровни прогресса (запущенная модель, корректные tool calls, проходящий код) нужно различать. Исследование носит эмпирический характер и не ранжирует модели и рантаймы.

en.title: Beyond Coherence: The Real Keys to Coding Success in ML Models
en.desc: This paper investigates the effectiveness of open-weight coding agents in generating successful code, emphasizing that success relies more on setup, protocol design, and behavioral checks than just text coherence. It presents empirical data from various coding sessions, highlighting differences in model performance based on tool-call formatting and context behavior. The findings reveal that while coherent text is important, it does not guarantee successful code execution or verification. The study provides a detailed account of the challenges and successes encountered in using different models for coding tasks, underscoring the importance of behavioral validation in machine learning applications.

zh.title: 成功编码的关键在于协议与验证
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了开放权重编码代理的实证研究，强调成功的代码生成不仅依赖于文本的一致性，还需要设置、协议设计和隐藏行为检查。研究表明，不同模型在工具调用格式、上下文行为和可靠性等方面存在差异，影响了编码的效果。通过对多个编码代理会话的分析，作者展示了直接编码和委托编码的成功率，并指出直接编码在成本效益上更具优势。最终，论文提供了关于代理协议、会话连续性和验证实践的实证证据。

papers.title: Mycelium: A Meta-Study of Hallucination Detection Across Provenance, Typology, and Granularities
papers.abstract: Abstract Hallucination detection is analyzed as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem across provenance, typology, and granularity axes, with a proposed Span Coverage F1 metric to address span-level evaluation variability.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Hallucination detection is increasingly important for evaluating and deploying large language models. However, existing methods are often compared across benchmarks that define and measure hallucination in substantially different ways, making reported scores difficult to interpret across settings. We study hallucination detection as a benchmark-conditioned measurement problem and organize existing benchmarks along three axes: provenance, which describes how model outputs and evidence conditions are obtained; typology, which captures the factuality and faithfulness failures represented by benchmark labels; and granularity, which specifies the unit at which hallucinations are annotated, predicted, and evaluated. Using this framework, we analyze how benchmark construction, annotation, and evaluation choices shape the underlying prediction task, and relate detector mechanisms and assumptions to the settings in which their performance is measured. We also examine span-level evaluation, where variation in annotation boundaries can substantially affect reported results, and propose Span Coverage F1 as a complementary containment-based metric. Our analysis clarifies what detector scores capture, highlights limitations of cross-benchmark comparisons, and motivates more explicit evaluation of generalization across benchmark conditions.

ru.title: Оценка детекции галлюцинаций LLM зависит от бенчмарка, и её нужно измерять честно
ru.desc: Статья рассматривает детекцию галлюцинаций LLM как задачу измерения, зависящую от бенчмарка, и классифицирует бенчмарки по трём осям: происхождение данных (provenance), типология ошибок (typology) и гранулярность разметки (granularity). Авторы показывают, как выбор способа построения и разметки датасетов влияет на саму задачу предсказания и на сравнимость результатов детекторов между разными бенчмарками. Отдельно исследуется оценка на уровне спанов, где различия в границах аннотаций заметно меняют итоговые метрики, и предлагается дополнительная метрика Span Coverage F1 на основе покрытия (containment). В целом работа помогает понять, что именно измеряют оценки детекторов, и призывает явнее оценивать обобщаемость методов между разными условиями бенчмарков.

en.title: Improving Hallucination Detection with Span Coverage F1
en.desc: This paper focuses on the challenge of detecting hallucinations in large language models, which are outputs that may not be factually accurate. It identifies that existing benchmarks for measuring hallucinations vary significantly in how they define and evaluate these errors, leading to confusion in interpreting results. The authors propose a new metric called Span Coverage F1 to improve evaluation consistency at the span level, addressing issues with how hallucinations are annotated and measured. By organizing benchmarks into categories based on provenance, typology, and granularity, the study aims to clarify the evaluation process and encourage better generalization across different benchmarks.

zh.title: 提升幻觉检测的评估标准
zh.desc: 本文分析了幻觉检测作为一种基准条件测量问题，涉及来源、类型和粒度三个维度。我们提出了一种新的Span Coverage F1指标，以解决在跨度级别评估中的变异性问题。现有的幻觉检测方法常常在定义和测量幻觉的基准上存在显著差异，导致不同设置下的得分难以比较。通过研究基准构建、注释和评估选择如何影响预测任务，我们强调了跨基准比较的局限性，并推动了对基准条件下泛化能力的更明确评估。

papers.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
papers.abstract: Abstract PAWM selectively predicts multi-step failures to guide black-box LLM agents away from pitfalls, improving performance via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement co-training.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.

ru.title: Предсказывай ошибки, а не каждое наблюдение: PAWM ведёт LLM-агента мимо ловушек
ru.desc: В статье представлен PAWM — world model для black-box LLM-агентов, которая не предсказывает следующее наблюдение на каждом шаге, а выборочно прогнозирует надвигающиеся ошибки (pitfalls) на ограниченном горизонте из нескольких шагов. Модель обучается в два этапа: сначала supervised fine-tuning на синтетических данных с размеченными ошибками, затем GRPO co-training с black-box LLM в целевой среде. Такой подход позволяет направлять агента в обход типичных ловушек и не тратить вычисления на избыточное прогнозирование. По результатам экспериментов PAWM повышает качество Claude Sonnet 4.5 на 24.3% в ScienceWorld и на 7.7% в WebArena-Lite.

en.title: Anticipating Pitfalls for Smarter LLM Agents
en.desc: The paper introduces the Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which enhances the performance of black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents by predicting multi-step failures. Unlike traditional world models that focus on predicting the next observation, PAWM selectively identifies potential pitfalls and intervenes to guide the agent away from them. This model is trained through a two-stage process involving supervised fine-tuning on synthetic data and reinforcement co-training with the LLM. The results show significant performance improvements in specific tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of PAWM in providing targeted guidance for LLM agents.

zh.title: PAWM：智能避开陷阱的世界模型
zh.desc: PAWM（陷阱预判世界模型）通过选择性预测多步失败，帮助黑箱大型语言模型（LLM）代理避免陷阱，从而提高性能。该模型通过监督微调和强化共同训练进行训练，能够在特定任务中提供环境特定的知识。与传统的世界模型不同，PAWM专注于预测潜在的失败，而不是每一步的观察，从而减少了不必要的计算成本。实验结果表明，PAWM在多个任务上显著提升了代理的表现，证明了其在黑箱LLM代理中的有效性。

papers.title: CRM-Agent-Bench: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents in Stateful Enterprise Environments
papers.abstract: Abstract The study introduces an execution-grounded benchmark for evaluating deployable language agents on multi-turn business tasks using strict contract-based success criteria across outcome, trajectory, viability, and compliance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Deploying language agents in real applications demands more than the right answer: an agent must execute a multi-step business process correctly, follow domain-specific rules, and interact with a user across a dialogue, where the gap between saying and doing is the gap between a satisfied customer and a real loss. We argue that a deployable-agent benchmark should jointly assess four facets: the outcome an agent reaches, the trajectory it takes, its operational viability, and its policy compliance. Customer relationship management (CRM), where mutable records meet operational rules and consequential effects, exercises all four. We introduce CRM-Agent-Bench, an execution-grounded benchmark of 555 stateful, multi-turn tasks across nine business domains and 36 capability tags. Each task supplies a task-specific executable contract drawn from checks over actions, arguments, order, response, target state, and protected state; success is the strict conjunction of the checks declared for that task. We evaluate the complete agent system through these contracts and report scored coverage, latency, and cost. Across sixteen systems evaluated on the audited final release, strict success spans 64.32% to 83.60%; the closely grouped leading systems nonetheless diverge sharply in cost and per-domain reliability. CRM-Agent-Bench offers an auditable framework for measuring contract-grounded business-transaction integrity and adherence to task-declared benchmark policies, with a portable structure designed for extension as models improve. Github repository: https://github.com/salesforce-misc/crm-agent-bench

ru.title: Агент должен не только ответить верно, но и правильно выполнить бизнес-процесс
ru.desc: В статье представлен CRM-Agent-Bench — бенчмарк на основе выполнения (execution-grounded) для оценки LLM-агентов в многошаговых бизнес-задачах с сохранением состояния. Каждая из 555 задач проверяется по исполняемому контракту: успех означает строгую конъюнкцию проверок действий, аргументов, порядка, ответа, целевого и защищённого состояния. Авторы оценивают не только результат, но и траекторию, операционную жизнеспособность (стоимость, задержку) и соблюдение политик, на примере CRM-систем. Для шестнадцати систем строгая успешность составила от 64.32% до 83.60%, при этом лидеры сильно различаются по стоимости и надёжности в разных доменах.

en.title: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World Business Success
en.desc: This paper presents a new benchmark called CRM-Agent-Bench for evaluating language agents in business tasks that require multi-turn dialogue. It emphasizes the importance of not just providing correct answers but also executing complex processes while adhering to specific rules and user interactions. The benchmark assesses agents based on four criteria: outcome, trajectory, viability, and compliance, ensuring a comprehensive evaluation of their performance. By using 555 tasks across various business domains, the study aims to improve the reliability and efficiency of deployable language agents in real-world applications.

zh.title: 评估可部署语言代理的执行基准
zh.desc: 本研究提出了一种基于执行的基准，用于评估可部署语言代理在多轮商业任务中的表现。评估标准包括结果、过程、可行性和合规性四个方面，确保代理不仅能给出正确答案，还能正确执行多步骤的业务流程。我们引入了CRM-Agent-Bench，这是一个包含555个状态保持的多轮任务的基准，涵盖九个商业领域和36个能力标签。通过这些任务的执行合同，我们可以全面评估代理系统的表现，包括覆盖率、延迟和成本等指标。

papers.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that predicts robot manipulation success from video frames using LoRA fine-tuning, calibrated token readouts, and source-specific regularization, achieving high accuracy and generalization across labs and robots.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at 2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.

ru.title: Робот сам скажет, выполнил ли он задачу, по видео
ru.desc: RoboJev-27B — это открытая vision-language model, которая по нескольким кадрам видео манипуляции и текстовой инструкции предсказывает, выполнил ли робот задачу. Модель получена дообучением JEV-27B-VL через LoRA-адаптер ранга 32 только для языковой части при замороженном vision encoder, с использованием source-specific KL-регуляризации, которая сохраняет близость предсказаний к исходной модели на исследовательских данных. Предсказание успеха/неудачи выполняется в один forward pass через калиброванное чтение двух токенов, что делает инференс быстрым и дешёвым. Модель показывает высокую точность (95.2% balanced accuracy на SO-101) и хорошо обобщается на эпизоды с неизвестных лабораторий и роботов, при этом авторы публикуют код и воспроизводимые результаты оценки.

en.title: Predicting Robot Success with Vision-Language Precision
en.desc: RoboJev-27B is a vision-language model designed to predict the success of robot manipulation tasks from video frames. It utilizes LoRA fine-tuning and calibrated token readouts to enhance its accuracy and generalization across different robots and labs. The model processes task instructions along with multiple frames from manipulation attempts to determine if the task was completed successfully. With impressive performance metrics, including a balanced accuracy of 95.2% and strong generalization capabilities, RoboJev-27B aims to improve the reliability of robot task evaluations.

zh.title: RoboJev-27B：机器人操作成功预测的先锋
zh.desc: RoboJev-27B 是一种开放权重的视觉-语言模型，能够从视频帧中预测机器人操作的成功率。它使用 LoRA 微调、校准的令牌输出和源特定正则化，达到了高准确率和良好的泛化能力。该模型能够处理任务指令和多个操作尝试的帧，并预测机器人是否成功完成任务。通过对52,598个实验记录的训练，RoboJev-27B 在不同实验室和机器人上都表现出色，具有很高的准确性和快速的推理速度。

papers.title: Constrained Decoding: Harmful or Beneficial? Revisiting Its Impact on LLM Performance
papers.abstract: Abstract Constrained decoding does not inherently harm reasoning; its effects depend on constraint type, with validity and reasoning constraints often improving reliability and accuracy by removing invalid paths.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Constrained decoding guarantees that Large Language Models (LLMs) produce outputs conforming to predefined formats, but is often assumed to inherently degrade reasoning. We examine this assumption through a taxonomy of three constraint types: format constraints, which enforce output structure; validity constraints, which mask invalid answer; and reasoning constraints, which restrict reasoning trajectories. We theoretically show that appropriate constraints can preserve or improve performance by eliminating invalid paths. Across four model families and eleven open-source models, causal ablations on diverse benchmarks using state-of-the-art constrained decoding strategies reveal that apparent performance degradation largely stems from non-equivalent prompting and output formats rather than from decoder-level masking. Meanwhile, validity constraints improve reliability and extractability by eliminating invalid answers, while reasoning constraints can improve reasoning and, consequently, accuracy when they enforce beneficial trajectories. These findings show that the impact of constrained decoding depends on the type of constraint and the output space it removes. Our code is available.
affiliations: Telecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, France

ru.title: Ограничения декодирования не губят рассуждения, если выбрать правильные
ru.desc: В статье исследуется, действительно ли constrained decoding (декодирование с ограничениями) ухудшает способность больших языковых моделей (LLM) к рассуждениям, как часто предполагается. Авторы вводят таксономию из трёх типов ограничений: форматные, валидационные и ограничения на траектории рассуждений, и теоретически показывают, что корректные ограничения могут сохранять или улучшать качество за счёт исключения невалидных путей генерации. Эксперименты на четырёх семействах моделей и одиннадцати open-source LLM показывают, что падение производительности обычно связано с неэквивалентными промптами и форматами вывода, а не с самим маскированием на уровне декодера. Валидационные ограничения повышают надёжность и извлекаемость ответов, а ограничения на рассуждения при правильной настройке улучшают точность, так что эффект зависит от типа ограничения.

en.title: Constrained Decoding: Enhancing Reasoning Through Smart Constraints
en.desc: This paper explores how constrained decoding in Large Language Models (LLMs) affects reasoning and output quality. It categorizes constraints into three types: format constraints that structure outputs, validity constraints that filter out invalid answers, and reasoning constraints that guide logical paths. The authors demonstrate that using the right constraints can enhance model performance by removing incorrect options rather than hindering reasoning. Their experiments show that performance issues often arise from prompting differences rather than the constraints themselves, highlighting the nuanced effects of different constraint types on model outputs.

zh.title: 约束解码：提升推理的关键
zh.desc: 约束解码并不一定会损害推理能力，其影响取决于约束类型。有效性约束和推理约束通常通过消除无效路径来提高可靠性和准确性。我们通过对三种约束类型的分类，理论上证明了适当的约束可以保持或提高模型性能。我们的实验结果表明，约束解码的影响与所移除的输出空间和约束类型密切相关。

papers.title: DialFork: Going Beyond Factuality to Evaluate Procedural Hallucination in Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract DialFork introduces a benchmark and flow-aware metrics to detect procedural hallucinations in conversational agents by measuring dialogue-level process deviation rather than content similarity.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) deployed as conversational agents are increasingly expected to follow procedural logic. While factual hallucination has received extensive attention, a different failure mode has been overlooked: procedural hallucination, in which an agent produces individually fluent and factually plausible utterances while deviating from the intended conversational process. We introduce DialFork, the first benchmark to measure this failure mode on raw dialogue text. DialFork is built by forking conformant dialogues at controlled turn positions and injecting one of four hallucination types, yielding 36,278 dialogues across 24 tasks in 12 domains; 30 human annotators validate the construction. We define three evaluation tasks that characterize procedural deviation at three granularities: how far a set of dialogues deviates from conformant ones (monitoring deployed agents), how far a single dialogue does (procedural retrieval), and at which turn a dialogue first goes off-track (real-time guardrails). For the first two, we propose dialog-flow-aware metrics, FlowKL and FlowScore, that compare dialogues by how they unfold rather than their content. At the dialogue level, FlowScore significantly outperforms all baselines across seven encoders, showing that semantic similarity is no substitute for procedural similarity. We release DialFork under the MIT license at https://github.com/idiap/dialfork, hoping the community will measure conversational process alongside content.

ru.title: Важен не только смысл ответа, но и путь диалога: измеряем процесс, а не только содержание
ru.desc: В статье представлен DialFork — первый бенчмарк для выявления процедурных галлюцинаций у разговорных AI-агентов на основе LLM, то есть ситуаций, когда ответы беглы и фактически правдоподобны, но нарушают заданный ход диалога. Авторы создали 36 278 диалогов, искусственно внося четыре типа галлюцинаций в корректные диалоги в контролируемых позициях, и привлекли 30 аннотаторов для валидации. Предложены метрики FlowKL и FlowScore, которые сравнивают диалоги по динамике их развития, а не по содержанию, и FlowScore значимо превосходит базовые методы на семи энкодерах. Авторы показывают, что семантическая схожесть не заменяет процедурную, и открывают датасет под лицензией MIT.

en.title: Measuring Conversational Flow: DialFork Unveils Procedural Hallucinations
en.desc: DialFork is a new benchmark designed to identify procedural hallucinations in conversational agents by focusing on how dialogues progress rather than just their content. It highlights a specific type of error where agents produce coherent and factually correct responses but stray from the intended conversational flow. The benchmark includes a large dataset of dialogues with various types of procedural deviations, validated by human annotators. Additionally, it introduces novel metrics, FlowKL and FlowScore, which effectively measure dialogue flow and outperform traditional content-based evaluations.

zh.title: 检测对话中的程序性幻觉
zh.desc: DialFork是一个新的基准，用于检测对话代理中的程序性幻觉，重点在于对话过程的偏差，而不是内容相似性。该研究提出了四种幻觉类型，并通过在控制的对话轮次中注入这些幻觉，生成了36,278个对话样本。我们定义了三种评估任务，以不同的粒度衡量程序性偏差，并提出了对话流感知的评估指标FlowKL和FlowScore。实验结果表明，FlowScore在对话级别上显著优于所有基线，强调了程序相似性的重要性。

papers.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
papers.abstract: Abstract RoboHarness enables LLM agents to perform embodied manipulation via a visual-geometric control interface, surpassing specialized vision-language-action models on robotics benchmarks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The rise of large language models (LLMs) has opened a path toward generalist embodied AI, raising the question of how LLMs can act in the physical world. One straightforward approach is training the model to generate actions: collect robot-action data and video demonstration, refine LLM architecture with an action head, and train a vision-language-action (VLA) model at scale. However, we argue that coding agents have the potential to realize generalist embodied manipulation. All they need is a simple yet effective robot harness. We present RoboHarness: a robotic harness that gives LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel so that they can directly understand and invoke embodied tasks. With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks. The implementation is open source.

ru.title: LLM-агенты умеют управлять роботами без специального обучения
ru.desc: Статья представляет RoboHarness — программную обвязку (harness), которая даёт LLM-агентам визуально-геометрический интерфейс управления для выполнения задач манипуляции роботом. Вместо обучения отдельной модели vision-language-action (VLA) с action head авторы показывают, что готовые кодирующие агенты могут напрямую понимать и вызывать физические действия через этот интерфейс. На бенчмарке BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 модель Qwen3.8-Flash-Next с RoboHarness превосходит специализированные state-of-the-art VLA-модели. Реализация выложена в открытый доступ.

en.title: Empowering LLMs with RoboHarness for Superior Robotic Control
en.desc: RoboHarness is a new tool that allows large language models (LLMs) to control robots in the physical world using a visual-geometric interface. Instead of relying solely on traditional vision-language-action (VLA) models, RoboHarness enables LLMs to directly understand and perform tasks by providing a simple control panel. This approach has shown to be more effective, as demonstrated by the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model outperforming existing VLA models on robotics benchmarks. The project is open source, promoting further research and development in embodied AI.

zh.title: RoboHarness：赋能 LLM 代理的机器人操作新工具
zh.desc: RoboHarness 是一种机器人控制工具，使大型语言模型（LLM）能够通过视觉几何控制界面进行物理操作。与专门的视觉-语言-动作模型相比，RoboHarness 在机器人基准测试中表现更佳。该工具允许 LLM 代理直接理解和执行具体任务，从而实现更通用的身体操作能力。RoboHarness 的实现是开源的，促进了机器人技术的发展。

papers.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
papers.abstract: Abstract GPT-6 Astra demonstrates partial capability across CAD workflows but remains limited by geometric validity, parametric dependencies, and assembly errors.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of CAD&CG, Zhejiang University, China

ru.title: AI уже помогает в CAD, но пока не заменит инженера
ru.desc: В статье проводится эмпирическое исследование GPT-6 Astra, универсальной LLM-модели уровня SOTA, на четырёх базовых задачах CAD: понимание модели, генерация, редактирование и оценка. Результаты показывают, что AI-модель уже поддерживает многие этапы CAD-процессов и справляется со сложной геометрией. Однако она часто создаёт правдоподобную на вид геометрию, которая не является валидной, функциональной и редактируемой, и допускает ошибки в свободной форме, параметрических зависимостях и сопряжениях деталей. Агентный итеративный подход улучшает результат, но не устраняет критические ошибки полностью, а долгое время выполнения ограничивает практическое применение.

en.title: Unlocking AI's Potential in CAD Workflows
en.desc: The paper evaluates GPT-6 Astra, a state-of-the-art AI model, in its ability to perform various tasks within computer-aided design (CAD) workflows. It assesses the model's performance in understanding, generating, editing, and evaluating CAD models through systematic testing. While GPT-6 Astra shows promise in handling complex geometric tasks, it struggles with maintaining geometric validity and managing parametric dependencies. The findings indicate that although general-purpose AI can assist in CAD processes, significant limitations remain that hinder its practical application in engineering.

zh.title: GPT-6 Astra：CAD工作流程中的新探索
zh.desc: 本文研究了GPT-6 Astra在计算机辅助设计（CAD）工作流程中的应用能力。尽管该模型在模型理解、生成、编辑和评估等基本CAD任务中表现出一定的能力，但仍存在几何有效性和参数依赖性等限制。研究表明，GPT-6 Astra能够支持CAD工作流程的多个阶段，但在生成有效和可编辑的CAD模型方面仍存在差距。通过迭代优化可以改善结果，但并不能始终解决关键错误，且较长的完成时间限制了其实际应用。

papers.title: Skill^{infty}: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract Skill∞ enables recursive self-improvement by letting a meta agent optimize both task skills and its own meta-skill through a reusable, agent-led procedure, improving performance across diverse domains.
